- [Now the First Instalment from Your Eggspert](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-08-16-batman-s-melbourne-now-the-first-instalment-from-your-eggspert/) — A Victorian Egg Board breakfast press event, at which board chairman Mr. Bain opens a seven-year-old shiny egg from his office to prove it has never gone bad, leads Keith Dunstan through egg storage science, egg-diet pamphlets calling for 26 eggs a week, and the calculation that eating 2370 million dozen eggs would absorb Australia's current wheat surplus and relieve John McEwen and the Country Party.
- [The Queue — A Kind of Cherished Tradition](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-08-23-batman-s-melbourne-the-queue-a-kind-of-cherished-tradition/) — Melbourne psychologist Leon Mann, now lecturing at Harvard, publishes his research on Melbourne's football-final ticket queues, finding that 25,000 people once waited a full week in mud for 12,500 tickets, that veterans regard queuing as a cherished ritual earning Agincourt-level kudos, and that organised scalpers flew Tasmanian students to Melbourne at $1 an hour to stand in line before reselling tickets at $35 apiece.
- [When the Queuing Has to Stop](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-09-13-batman-s-melbourne-when-the-queuing-has-to-stop/) — This year's MCG grand-final ticket queue disintegrates at 2 a.m. in a fist-fight that sends eight people to hospital and leaves two days of bottles and rubbish to clean up, reviving the annual question of whether tickets should be sold by mail, handed to clubs for distribution among worthy members, or, Keith Dunstan's modest proposal, by broadcasting all finals from a secret location in Alice Springs on coaxial cable.
- [Dishing It Out to the Waiters](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-09-20-batman-s-melbourne-dishing-it-out-to-the-waiters/) — Keith Dunstan judges the Victorian elimination of the national wine waiter contest at the Royal Commonwealth Society in Queen's Road, where contestants must serve imaginary meals for Lady Clarke, Bert Newton, and jockey Geoff Lane while being docked points for imperfect shoes, failure to open bottles in full view, and serving in the wrong direction, until a winner is found who passes the shiraz-versus-hermitage test and whose breath contains not a hint of garlic.
- [In Defence of the Charismatic Meat Pie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-09-27-batman-s-melbourne-in-defence-of-the-charismatic-meat-pie/) — Sydney editorial attacks on the Australian Tourist Commission for flying meat pies to Tokyo provoke Keith Dunstan to defend Melbourne's two million pies a week, propose a national pie secretariat modelled on the wool promotion board, and produce an imaginary 1869 dialogue in which Tina Carr explains to her husband Graham that the attic of air in his pie is her own invention to keep it hot and fresh.
- [A City That Loves to Be Disdained](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-10-04-batman-s-melbourne-a-city-that-loves-to-be-disdained/) — British architectural critic J. M. Richards, editor of the 'Architectural Review' and guest of Robin Boyd and Neil Clerehan, tours Melbourne's new buildings and dispatches them in turn, the AMP tower 'dung-brown,' the Masonic Centre 'too dressed up,' the Arts Centre 'too many gimmicks,' the National Mutual building 'too fancy,' the ICI building 'fine but could be anywhere', to the city's deep delight.
- [There's No Future in Being a Star](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-10-11-batman-s-melbourne-theres-no-future-in-being-a-star/) — Melbourne's new tabloid evening newspaper Newsday launches with 450,000 copies on its first day, its columnists including Zara Holt and Harry Beitzel, and a column named for John Pascoe Fawkner, prompting Keith Dunstan to compare it with the 1933 Melbourne Star, the Argus's tabloid evening experiment that sold 26,000 on its first day, rose to 62,000, and folded after three years.
- [Vice Is a Four-Letter Word](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-10-18-batman-s-melbourne-vice-is-a-four-letter-word/) — A letter from a bewildered Czech migrant who cannot discover which words Melbourne's vice squad will prosecute leads Keith Dunstan to defend the antiquity of Anglo-Saxon swear words against their proposed suppression, propose National Trust classification for the better ones, and then travel to the Society of Experimental Test Pilots' symposium at the Beverly Hills Hilton, where Neil Armstrong, Alan Shepard, Wally Schirra and Gordon Cooper mix star-power lunches with talk of zero-gravity welding and the quarantine YMCA's Sears Spanish furniture.
- [Immortalising a Rabbit Warren](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-10-25-batman-s-melbourne-immortalising-a-rabbit-warren/) — The National Trust's acquisition of Barwon Park, the 42-room bluestone mansion near Winchelsea built by squatter Thomas Austin who released 24 rabbits from the clipper Lightning in 1859, leads Keith Dunstan through Eric Rolls's account of how the English rabbit adapted magnificently to antipodean conditions, the Duke of Edinburgh's record bag of 86 rabbits in a morning, and a proposal for a bronze memorial to those first two bunnies.
- [All Tied Up with Respectability](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-11-01-batman-s-melbourne-all-tied-up-with-respectability/) — The backlash against hippy informality has produced a black-tie boom in Melbourne with five formal invitations arriving per week and 130 dress-hire establishments now listed in the pink pages, where Mrs. Belle Benjamin reports the dress-hire business has trebled in three years, leading Keith Dunstan to propose a union of non-formal-wear wearers called the Angry Penguins with Max Harris as patron.
- [How to Put Our Trust in the Forgettable](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-11-08-batman-s-melbourne-how-to-put-our-trust-in-the-forgettable/) — An article by Sydney architect David Young criticising Melbourne's built environment, ending with the flashing Carlton Brewery sign as the city's true glory, inspires Keith Dunstan to found the National Distrust of Australia, a parody body that grades ugly buildings for preservation rather than lovely ones, with the Carlton Brewery sign earning an A classification and Whelan the Wrecker as the proposed foreword writer for its coffee-table companion volume.
- [You Can't Strike a Good God Down](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-11-15-batman-s-melbourne-you-can-t-strike-a-good-god-down/) — The 1969 Melbourne Cup is nearly wrecked when the Railways Union and Tramways Union threaten to stop the special trains and trams to Flemington, the bank clerks call a Monday strike, and the Trades Hall Council places a black ban on all TAB sporting fixtures, until Chief Secretary Arthur Rylah cuts short an oil-rig inspection tour to negotiate a settlement, Sir Paul Hasluck arrives in a Rolls-Royce in top hat and tails, and 85,000 faithful attend the religious festival undisturbed.
- [Let's Not Cry Over Spilt Beer — Do Something](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-11-22-batman-s-melbourne-lets-not-cry-over-spilt-beer-do-something/) — New international hotels are rising across Melbourne, the Southern Cross extension, a 40-storey Austin Anderson project, a 37-storey William Street proposal, while more than 30 old pubs have closed since 1938, including the labyrinthine Port Phillip Club, the Occidental with its bar later hired for the film 'On the Beach' where Ava Gardner leaned against it, and the Lord Clyde, prompting Keith Dunstan's call to preserve one last authentic Melbourne pub with dung-coloured lino and a haunting smell of urine.
- [Steamrollering — Ah, Those Were the Days](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-11-29-batman-s-melbourne-steamrollering-ah-those-were-the-days/) — The Melbourne Steam Traction Club's rally at Wantirna, featuring six fully operating rollers and traction engines including a magnificent 1906 Foden Compound Traction Engine owned by John Smyth of Ringwood, revives Keith Dunstan's childhood passion for steamrollers suppressed since councils replaced Aveling and Porter machines with soulless diesel rollers in the 1950s, and leads to a road test of the 1924 Fowler 6 hp Compound whose bad points include a wheel requiring 45 turns before it ponders altering course.
- [Summer Madness](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/walkabout-magazine/1969/summer-madness/) — A wry survey of Australia's overloaded summer beach culture, surfboards, caravans, and competitive Rosebud campsites, from Portsea and Palm Beach's Toorak-set glamour to Surfers Paradise's Miami-style tower blocks.
- [At Last, a Bridge: Symbol of Natural Modesty](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-12-06-batman-s-melbourne-at-last-a-bridge-symbol-of-natural-modesty/) — The West Gate Bridge, costing $42 million and already half finished, gives Melbourne the thumbprint it has always lacked, with its main span of 1000 feet, height of 176 feet above the Yarra's piddling 200 yards, and eight 12-foot lanes quietly surpassing the Sydney Harbour Bridge on every specification except main span length, while Sir Henry Bolte, presented with a silver-plated axe at the 1968 ground-breaking, declared it blunt and denied being a hatchet man.
- [It's Time to Appeal for Fair Play and Decency](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-12-13-batman-s-melbourne-its-time-to-appeal-for-fair-play-and-decency/) — The Albert Park Lake weed Elodea canadensis has driven the rowing club to the Yarra, the yacht club to despair and the power boat club to Lake Eppalock, despite $60,000 spent over ten years on copper sulphate, a $5000 English weed-cutting boat that only distributed the growth, Senator Kennelly's rejected proposal to import South American manatees, and a yabbie scheme abandoned when universities and fishermen offered three times the purchase price, leading Keith Dunstan to suggest appealing to the weed's sense of decency and fair play.
- [Getting to Know the World's Really Rich](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1969/1969-12-27-batman-s-melbourne-getting-to-know-the-worlds-really-rich/) — The official opening of the AMP Society's new 26-storey William Street tower, built over the demolished St. James Building by Skidmore Owings and Merrill with local architects Bates Smart and McCutcheon, reveals 26,400 square feet of travertine marble, a staff basement with five billiard tables, a gymnasium, four table tennis tables and a squash court, and a $50,000 sculpture by Clement Meadmore that has already been defaced by graffiti enthusiasts treating it like a urinal.
- [That Was the Year That Was 1970](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-01-03-batman-s-melbourne-that-was-the-year-that-was-1970/) — A satirical prediction column for Melbourne in 1970, forecasting the Tullamarine Airport opening, Sir Henry Bolte's election strategy, a disappointing VFL season, the "Hair" and "Oh! Calcutta!" controversies, the mining boom, the fashion industry's maxi-skirt battle, and the general human comedy of city life.
- [Jazzing Up the Dear Old George](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-01-10-batman-s-melbourne-jazzing-up-the-dear-old-george/) — A report on the 24th Australian Jazz Convention, held over five days at the George Hotel in Ballarat, where 450 jazz lovers from across the continent took over the Victorian-era hotel for round-the-clock sessions, marches, and improvised mayhem.
- [Skipping Around a Rewarding Tragedy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-01-17-batman-s-melbourne-skipping-around-a-rewarding-tragedy/) — A review of D. L. Bernstein's social history of the Melbourne Cup, "First Tuesday in November," tracing the race from its origins under Captain Standish through the legends of Archer, Poseidon and Jimmy Ah Poon, and celebrating the Cup's role in Australian national life.
- [The Night I Was Kept Awake by a Belly Dancer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-02-07-batman-s-melbourne-the-night-i-was-kept-awake-by-a-belly-dancer/) — A TV nightmare about automated television broadcasting leads into a genuine account of surviving an HSV-7 movie marathon from midnight to 8 a.m., taking in Humphrey Bogart, Mel Ferrer's possessed strangling hands, Modigliani's death scene, and the redeeming glory of Laurel and Hardy in "The Blockheads."
- [This Game's Nearly as Bad as Aussie Rules](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-02-14-batman-s-melbourne-this-games-nearly-as-bad-as-aussie-rules/) — A dispatch from the Melbourne Stock Exchange gallery during the Poseidon mining boom, comparing the feverish broking-floor atmosphere to barracking at the MCG, and gently mocking the euphemistic language finance writers reach for when the market gets nervous.
- [There's Something to Be Said for the Old John Bull](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-02-21-batman-s-melbourne-theres-something-to-be-said-for-the-old-john-bull/) — As Melbourne prepares for the 1970 royal tour, Keith examines a surprising royalist revival led by Brigadier Richard Eason's British Brotherhood, which seeks one flag, one anthem and a common Commonwealth defence, while Myer stages a British week complete with a Santa Claus dressed as John Bull.
- [A Man with Real Power Behind His Attack](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-02-28-batman-s-melbourne-a-man-with-real-power-behind-his-attack/) — A profile of William O. Bourke, managing director of Ford Motor Company of Australia, who has launched a public campaign blaming politicians rather than car makers for Australia's road toll, and who proposes a 10-point plan including better roads, tougher licensing, real punitive measures for drunk drivers, and the abolition of trams.
- [Just the Shot for Mad Dogs and Englishmen](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-03-07-batman-s-melbourne-just-the-shot-for-mad-dogs-and-englishmen/) — A war-correspondent account of joining the opening day of the duck shooting season in the Riverina near Hay, where 100-plus camouflaged gunmen mobilise before dawn through swamp mud, with pre-battle keg, army-surplus logistics, and a dog so faithful it kept retrieving the one protected water hen someone shot by mistake.
- [Boys Will Be Boys — or Is It a Girl?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-03-14-batman-s-melbourne-boys-will-be-boys-or-is-it-a-girl/) — A Geelong court case in which a young man assaulted someone he took to be a boy prompts a field guide to identifying the sexes in the age of unisex fashion, covering make-up, hair, footwear, trousers and handbags, with a final tip borrowed from James Laver that the creature acting like the boss is almost certainly female.
- [If You've Got Wine, Who Needs Women and Song?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-03-21-batman-s-melbourne-if-youve-got-wine-who-needs-women-and-song/) — A report on the Rutherglen Wine Festival, which drew 20,000 visitors to a town of 1600, featuring free wine at the wineries, a street procession with a working still on the back of a truck, a barrel-rolling contest, hay-bale singing under the stars, and the election of a Vintage Queen from candidates including Miss Riesling, Miss Port and Miss Claret.
- [Once Upon a Time — or Things Could Be Better](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-03-28-batmans-melbourne-once-upon-a-time-or-things-could-be-better/) — A rueful reckoning with Melbourne's reputation, prompted by Opposition leader Clyde Holding calling the city 'the little Chicago' after a run of murders, armed hold-ups and kidnappings, set against the city's traditional pride in its Sunday decorum and its virtuous contrast with Sydney.
- [A Night in the Clink for the National Trust](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-04-04-batman-s-melbourne-a-night-in-the-clink-for-the-national-trust/) — The National Trust throws a champagne party inside the condemned Melbourne Gaol, as rival plans for Pentridge Prison and proposals for a $40 million redevelopment leave Melbourne's most magnificently horrible jails facing uncertain futures.
- [Bendigo's Magic Dragon Gives Its Last Puff](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-04-11-batman-s-melbourne-bendigos-magic-dragon-gives-its-last-puff/) — The centenary of Bendigo's Easter Fair Parade brings two dragons into the streets, Old Loong making his final public appearance after nearly a century, and a magnificent new 200-foot dragon, Sun Loong, arriving from Hong Kong to take his place.
- [See What Happens When Rules Become a Religion](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-04-18-batmans-melbourne-see-what-happens-when-rules-become-a-religion/) — The opening of the VFL football season reveals a new industrial mood among players, with strikes at Collingwood and Essendon over pay, prompting speculation about a Footballers' Association of Victoria aligned with the ACTU.
- [I'm in the Moog for Love](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-04-25-batmans-melbourne-im-in-the-moog-for-love/) — Melbourne jingle-maker Bruce Clarke demonstrates his newly acquired $12,000 Moog synthesiser, the electronic marvel capable of creating any sound on earth, from Arctic blizzards to canaries singing Twinkle Twinkle Little Star with an elastic band accompaniment.
- [The Way to Make a Million in Australiana](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-05-02-batman-s-melbourne-the-way-to-make-a-million-in-australiana/) — Melbourne goes mad for Australiana-themed restaurants and bars, with the Hotel Australia's Wool Shed, the Commodore Motel's Eureka Stockade complex, and the Branding Iron all opening within weeks of each other, leading Keith Dunstan to announce his own Instant Australiana Mart.
- [Batman at Botany Bay Where It Looked as if Cook Discovered a Used-Car Yard](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-05-09-batman-at-botany-bay-where-it-looked-as-if-cook-discovered-a-used-car-yard/) — Keith Dunstan travels to Sydney for the Captain Cook bicentenary celebrations, finding Kurnell choked with cars and plastic pennants, a re-enactment hampered by failed electronics, and the Aboriginal community at La Perouse watching the festivities with a complicated grief.
- [Where Bad Weather's Best to Ride Mountains That Move](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-05-16-batman-s-melbourne-where-bad-weathers-best-to-ride-mountains-that-move/) — The World Surfing Championships at Bell's Beach near Geelong draw 80 competitors from 18 countries, with Midget Farrelly the finest artist on the waves, and the event saved from cancellation only by Sir Henry Bolte backing it with $22,000 weeks before the state election.
- [What's Mr. Playboy Doing in a Dedman Suit?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-05-23-batman-s-melbourne-whats-mr-playboy-doing-in-a-dedman-suit/) — Playboy's men's fashion director Robert L. Green visits Melbourne to show how the magazine covers male style, but arrives wearing a dull grey Dedman suit and a wide paisley tie, confirming that Australian fashion lags three years behind New York.
- [What a Beautiful Baby Is Leading the Pre-Poll Parade](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-05-30-batman-s-melbourne-what-a-beautiful-baby-is-leading-the-pre-poll-parade/) — In the weeks before the Victorian state election, a rush of government announcements, from the South Eastern Freeway extension to new trains and a tower hotel beside the Regent Theatre, illustrates how the pre-poll season resembles football's heady opening round of optimism.
- [Oh, for the Return of the Eminent Dr. Clutterbuck](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-06-06-batman-s-melbourne-oh-for-the-return-of-the-eminent-dr-clutterbuck/) — The decision to demolish the Regent Theatre and replace it with a 53-storey hotel and office tower signals the end of the Paris End of Collins Street, as the accelerating destruction of the city's nineteenth-century buildings proceeds from the Coates ice-cube tray to the Oriental Hotel.
- [Now Is the Time for All Good Men to Come to the Aid of Their Trousers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-06-13-batman-s-melbourne-now-is-the-time-for-all-good-men-to-come-to-the-aid-of-their-/) — Melbourne's male-only pub culture crumbles as the new Eureka Stockade tavern throws open all its bars to women, tracing a long history from colonial mateship and female shortages through to the last bastions at Flemington's Members Stand and the Melbourne Club.
- [Ho, Yo-Yo and a Bottle of Coke](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-06-20-batman-s-melbourne-ho-yo-yo-and-a-bottle-of-coke/) — A Coca-Cola sponsored yo-yo promotion at the Southern Cross Hotel gives Keith Dunstan occasion to mourn the passing of spontaneous childhood hobbies, from hula hoops and go-carts to silkworms and cigarette cards.
- [The Wit of a Man Cartoonists Would Hate to Lose](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-06-27-batman-s-melbourne-the-wit-of-a-man-cartoonists-would-hate-to-lose/) — A pocket compendium of Sir Henry Bolte's most quotable remarks, assembled after his crushing 1970 election victory, argues that his deadpan bluntness deserves its own volume alongside Churchill and Menzies.
- [You Get One-Third Less at Tullamarine](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-07-04-batman-s-melbourne-you-get-one-third-less-at-tullamarine/) — A comparison of the newly opened Tullamarine Airport with Sydney's Kingsford Smith finds Melbourne's terminal consistently one-third smaller in every measure, from baggage carousels and immigration desks to souvenir koalas and VIP lounges.
- [When Is a Floor Not a Floor? When It's a Living Experience](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-07-11-batman-s-melbourne-when-is-a-floor-not-a-floor-when-its-a-living-experience/) — Two new exhibitions at Melbourne galleries, an undulating timber floor built from Whelan the Wrecker salvage at Gallery A in South Yarra and a Philip Morris air-themed show at the National Gallery, test Keith Dunstan's willingness to take conceptual art seriously.
- [Down in the Depths About Going Up in the Air](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-08-22-batman-s-airways-down-in-the-depths-about-going-up-in-the-air/) — A world tour of airports, culminating at Boeing's vast Everett factory outside Seattle, finds the jumbo jet age transforming air travel into an exhausting exercise in walking while making the aircraft themselves look like ocean liners coming in to berth.
- [The Ambition of Mr Five Percent](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-08-29-batman-s-melbourne-the-ambition-of-mr-five-percent/) — Ford Australia's announcement that Brian Inglis would become its first Australian managing director, and that the outgoing chief William Bourke would head a new Asia-Pacific division, prompts a meditation on fast cars, road safety, and the peculiar ambitions of a man aiming for the top of one of the world's great corporations.
- [Taxes That Take the Fun Out of Life](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-09-05-batman-s-melbourne-taxes-that-take-the-fun-out-of-life/) — The federal budget's new wine tax prompts an elegy for the great Melbourne tradition of home bottling, with Dan Murphy lamenting the death blow to a joyous, laughing industry, while Keith Dunstan proposes compensating taxes on yoghurt, rosehips and Coca-Cola to make the wowsers pay their share.
- [All Boys in the Ban, But for a Naughty Neighbor](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-09-12-batman-s-melbourne-all-boys-in-the-ban-but-for-a-naughty-neighbor/) — Victoria's struggle to maintain public decency is undermined at every turn by South Australia, where Don Dunstan allows 'Portnoy's Complaint' to be sold, wears shorts to Parliament and presides over the longest drinking hours in Australia, prompting Keith Dunstan to quote at length a Victorian preacher's Victorian-era pamphlet on the perils of self-pollution.
- [Behind Bars — It Just Happened That Way](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-09-19-batmans-mildura-behind-bars-it-just-happened-that-way/) — A visit to the Mildura Workingman's Club, which claims the world's longest bar at 295 feet and 8 inches, reveals an institution that has grown from a modest beginning into a vast complex of restaurants, a floor-cabaret, a billiard room and a boardroom fitted with a sliding bar, all for a $2 annual subscription.
- [Burning Sir Henry at Both Ends](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-09-26-batman-s-melbourne-burning-sir-henry-at-both-ends/) — Melbourne's 16 major electricity stoppages since May 1969 have turned candle-shopping into a civic pastime, with the most popular model being a 99-cent effigy of Sir Henry Bolte's head, while Keith Dunstan traces the city's industrial action tradition to the great Victorian Railways strike of May 1903.
- [Depravity in the Crucible of Prudery](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-10-03-batman-s-melbourne-depravity-in-the-crucible-of-prudery/) — A review of two recently translated nineteenth-century novels set in colonial Victoria, including the memoirs-turned-fiction of French courtesan Celeste de Chabrillan, whose lurid account of the Melbourne gold rush depicted the colony as a place of rape, murder and depravity.
- [A Time When Ladies Can Become Gentlemen](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-10-10-batman-s-melbourne-a-time-when-ladies-can-become-gentlemen/) — The 1970 VFL Grand Final, won by Carlton, is examined through the flood of newspaper supplements, the record-breaking crowd of 121,696, scalpers charging up to $60 a seat, and the curious instance of men removing their make-up to gain admission through the MCG's ladies' reserve.
- [Flashpoints on the Bunyip's Intimate Parts](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-10-17-batman-s-melbourne-flashpoints-on-the-bunyips-intimate-parts/) — A private screening of John Murray's censored documentary film 'The Naked Bunyip' at the Palais Theatre, with the censored passages flagged by coloured lamps, reveals the contradictions of Australian film censorship in 1970, from pack rape to Barry Humphries, prostitutes and a toothpaste commercial.
- [Would You Believe Tourists for the Quaffing Of](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-10-24-batman-s-vineyards-would-you-believe-tourists-for-the-quaffing-of/) — Two ambitious new vineyard developments, the Rothbury Estate in the Hunter Valley and the Michelton winery on the Goulburn River, are building tourist hotels and tasting rooms to attract wine-loving visitors in the manner of the great European wine regions.
- [One Ray of Sunshine Threatens a Reputation](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-10-31-batman-s-melbourne-one-ray-of-sunshine-threatens-a-reputation/) — A week of unusually withering comment about Melbourne, from a visiting Clement Freud who called it an ideal city for escaping Dartmoor, to Robin Boyd lamenting the loss of creative spirit in its architecture, and Barry Humphries delivering a fond but cutting ode to its musical-comedy qualities, prompts Keith Dunstan to wonder whether becoming internationally understood will cost Melbourne its carefully nourished reputation.
- [A Sacred Day in a City of Light](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-11-14-batman-s-melbourne-a-sacred-day-in-a-city-of-light/) — The 1970 Melbourne Cup, won by Baghdad Note, becomes the occasion for a survey of the day's religious significance in Australian life, the government's hasty legislation after Myer tried to open its stores on Show Day, the Flemington fashion parade in what looked like Baghdad-inspired costume, and the strange segregation of the MCG Members' Stand replicated at VRC.
- [Will Little Audrey Skip on for Ever?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-11-21-batman-s-melbourne-will-little-audrey-skip-on-for-ever/) — The return of the Skipping Girl Vinegar sign to Abbotsford, celebrated by Barry Humphries in verse, prompts a wider survey of the National Trust's classification system and a plea to extend it under 'Batman's Law' to the State Theatre, Flinders Street Station, the Exhibition Building fountain, and even the small iron pissoir at Flinders and Exhibition Streets.
- [Not So Much an Airport, More a Lovely Nightmare](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-11-28-batman-s-melbourne-not-so-much-an-airport-more-a-lovely-nightmare/) — Five months after opening, Tullamarine Airport receives a detailed architectural verdict, with the Victorian chapter of the Royal Australian Institute of Architects finding outstanding individual elements undermined by poor co-ordination, while the new TraveLodge tri-arc hotel next door already looks lonely in its green paddocks.
- [The Man in the Plastic Ball Wants to Take Away the Blonde](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-12-05-batman-s-melbourne-the-man-in-the-plastic-ball-wants-to-take-away-the-blonde/) — The opening of Neptune's Fish Bowl, a fish-and-chip shop on Toorak Road surmounted by a 20-foot fibreglass ball lit to suggest the sea, features a mermaid whose fish scales fall off during the ceremony and a Neptune whose goldfish nearly expires in the heat, raising the question of whether Melbourne's beloved Greek flake-and-chips culture can survive the arrival of upmarket 'take-away seafood.'
- [Camping Among Cairns of Cans at the Gabba](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-12-12-batman-s-brisbane-camping-among-cairns-of-cans-at-the-gabba/) — The First Test between Australia and England at the Woolloongabba in Brisbane, watched by shirtless crowds sitting in armchairs amid cairns of empty beer cans and piles of prawn shells, offers a scene of magnificent Australian informality that the country's coffee-table books have been too snobbish to document.
- [Gone Is the Nudists' Favourite Privacy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1970/1970-12-19-batman-s-gold-coast-gone-is-the-nudists-favorite-privacy/) — A Christmas visit to Surfers Paradise reveals the Broadbeach International hotel remodelled in Spanish and Mexican theme bars, a revolving giant beer mug on the main strip, and Marineland's new killer whale shipped from Seattle at great expense, while the nudists' favourite dunes have been turned into a tourist aquatic park.
- [Now Here's a Dame Who Slept Around](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-01-02-batman-s-melbourne-now-heres-a-dame-who-slept-around/) — A lament for four Melbourne institutions closing at once, the Oriental Hotel at the Paris end of Collins Street, the Regent Theatre with its Vintage Hoyts decor, the Tasma Guest House in Parliament Place, and Hilliers milk bar by the Regent, all falling to wreckers over the Christmas break.
- [Talking Turkey with the Rosebuddies](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-01-09-batmans-melbourne-talking-turkey-with-the-rosebuddies/) — A Christmas visit to the Rosebud camping strip on Port Phillip Bay finds Melbourne's herd instinct on vivid display, with caravans equipped with double beds, air-conditioning and walkie-talkies, and the regulars boasting they haven't missed a season in 45 years.
- [The Woeful Fat Man Says It's a Glorious Climate](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-01-16-batman-s-melbourne-the-woeful-fat-man-says-its-a-glorious-climate/) — Melbourne's notorious weather, which wrecked an entire Test Match and drew comment from Robert Menzies, inspires a dossier of celebrated complaints reaching back to 1863, from Ellen Kean to Marcus Clarke's 'Glorious Climate' monologue.
- [What Next to Expect from Sex](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-01-23-batman-s-melbourne-what-next-to-expect-from-sex/) — A survey of the sex creeping into Melbourne's comic strips, fairy tales, Collins Book Depot's bestseller lists, and even the rejuvenated Sexton Blake detective series, concluding that the day cannot be far off before someone publishes a sex book by Malcolm Muggeridge.
- [Shandy: a Menace or a Mockery?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-01-30-batman-s-melbourne-shandy-a-menace-or-a-mockery/) — Cooper's Brewery launches a two percent alcohol shandy in a gold ring-top can, prompting outrage from church groups, stern warnings from school mothers' clubs, and the alarming prospect that Carlton and United might buy up milk bars all over the country and give them mock-Tudor fronts.
- [The Pharters on the Hill Know the Game's Lovely Ritual Qualities](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-02-27-batman-s-melbourne-the-pharters-on-the-hill-know-the-games-lovely-ritual-qualiti/) — A defence of Test cricket's solemn ritual against calls to brighten it up, arguing that its magnificent, unalterable dullness is its greatest charm, drawing on statistics from W. L. Murdoch in 1881 and a comparison with Chinese Opera as evidence that nothing has ever really happened and nothing ever will.
- [Alexandra the Great Says It's Hard for a Real Exotic Dancer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-03-06-batmans-melbourne-alexandra-the-great-says-its-hard-for-a-real-exotic-dancer/) — For Moomba, Ferdinand Nemeth's club El Toro Espana in Russell Street has imported Alexandra the Great, billed as possessing the world's biggest bust, and Keith Dunstan goes backstage to talk with the St. Louis-born Geraldine Paredes about the decline of proper exotic dancing in an era when a girl who will take off all her clothes straight off the street is considered sufficient.
- [Will the Man in the Abstract Painting Be the Model of the Year?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-03-13-batman-s-melbourne-will-the-man-in-the-abstract-painting-be-the-model-of-the-yea/) — A Suave menswear fashion parade at the Savoy Plaza Hotel presents the 1971 look, a riot of knickerbockers, hot pants for men, burgundy shirts and striped overalls, leading Keith Dunstan to stand alone in anxiously awaiting the resurgence of blue serge.
- [Give the Disreputable Flag to the Pentridge Graduate, Said Phelan](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-03-20-batman-s-melbourne-give-the-disreputable-flag-to-the-pentridge-graduate-said-phe/) — The history of Melbourne's St Patrick's Day processions, from the triumphs of Archbishop Mannix and his fourteen Victoria Cross winners in 1920 to the 1971 edition, which has been reduced to a Summer Happening at the Myer Music Bowl with proceeds to the Yooralla School.
- [Would the Young Males Step Forward, Please?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-03-27-batman-s-melbourne-would-the-young-males-step-forward-please/) — With Australia apparently devoting a quarter of its female population under 21 to beauty contests, Keith Dunstan wonders why charities have entirely overlooked young males as contestants, who are surely equally deserving of trips around the world, dream automatic sedans, and free hairdos.
- [How the Pure Sunday Disappeared in Melbourne](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-04-03-batman-s-melbourne-how-the-pure-sunday-disappeared-in-melbourne/) — The 1971 Melbourne Sunday newspaper wars, in which the Sunday Observer folds and is replaced almost overnight by the Melbourne Observer under Max Newton, leaving readers hunting half a dozen milk bars to assemble a complete cover, and the managing director of the Sunday Review cautiously optimistic about the quarter million Melburnians who will still buy Sunday papers.
- [Wrong Bishop Wronged](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-04-03-wrong-bishop-wronged/) — A letter from M. E. Ryan of St Kilda correcting Batman's Melbourne of 20 March 1971, which misidentified Bishop Phelan as the administrator of the Melbourne diocese in 1921, explaining that the Very Reverend John Barry held that role, and that Phelan had severed his connection with the archdiocese in 1913.
- [How to Be a Stylish Gold Digger Without Getting Your Feet Muddy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-04-10-batman-s-melbourne-how-to-be-a-stylish-gold-digger-without-getting-your-feet-mud/) — A tour of Victoria's competing goldfield tourist towns, from Wedderburn's fossicking pond to Ballarat's Sovereign Hill historical park, where the gold is purchased from a bank and the dunny wall is already growing honeysuckle.
- [Spartan Discipline and Twenty Push-Ups for the Dedicated](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-04-17-batmans-melbourne-spartan-discipline-and-twenty-push-ups-for-the-dedicated/) — The opening week of the 1971 VFL season, dominated by the Ron Barassi and Adrian Gallagher push-up affair at Carlton and by Brian Dixon's North Melbourne pulling off a stunning upset over the reigning premiers.
- [Peaches and Cream in a Soulful Setting](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-04-24-batmans-melbourne-peaches-and-cream-in-a-soulful-setting/) — A report on Cobram's inaugural Peaches and Cream Festival, a Murray River pop and folk event at Easter that combined an Apex-run stage on army pontoons, a cyclone-fence perimeter, five speedboats watching for drownees, and a Channel Nine crew egging on a brawl.
- [Those Very Daring Young Men in Their Flying Machines](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-05-01-batman-s-melbourne-those-very-daring-young-men-in-their-flying-machines/) — An account of the RAAF's 50th anniversary air pageant at Laverton, comparing the nostalgic spectacle of pre-war Bristol Bulldog aerobatics with the terrifying head-on chicken runs of Macchi jets, Mirages and Phantoms before a crowd that shut the Geelong road for two hours.
- [And How Much Can Yaha Bibi Deduct for Bed Linen?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-05-08-batmans-melbourne-and-how-much-can-yaha-bibi-deduct-for-bed-linen/) — A survey of income-tax guides for the approaching end of the financial year, including a book that addresses deductions available to prostitutes, a 1952 Cairo Supreme Court case classifying three simultaneous 'stipending friends' as proof of professional income, and the grand days of Madame Brussels in Lonsdale Street.
- [Copper Bed-Warmers, Black Satin Nighties and Other Bits of Nostalgia](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-05-15-batman-s-melbourne-copper-bed-warmers-black-satin-nighties-and-other-bits-of-nos/) — Melbourne's competitive nostalgia industry, from a South Yarra gallery showing the history of bed-warming devices to the new Old Melbourne Motor Inn at Flemington Road fitted out with chandeliers from the demolished Regent Theatre, and the National Trust's campaign to raise the HMVS Cerebus from Black Rock.
- [Aeroplanes](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-05-22-batman-s-aeroplanes/) — A review of the illustrated history 'Aircraft of the RAAF 1921-71', moving through five decades of types from DH9 biplanes and Westland Wapitis to Catalina flying-boats and the CA-15, and concluding that the most beautiful aircraft the RAAF ever possessed was the de Havilland Mosquito.
- [Melbourne Keeps Its 'Hair' On](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-06-05-batman-s-melbourne-melbourne-keeps-its-hair-on/) — A report on opening night of the musical 'Hair' at Melbourne's Metro Theatre, where the audience dressed as gurus and swamis outnumbered ordinary patrons, Ron Barassi attended in the front row, and Harry Miller's post-show mystery buses toured the city before arriving at a whitewashed Fitzroy dairy showing Judy Garland films and Carmen Miranda.
- [An Old Lover Turns Faithless, and It's Not the Same Anymore](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-06-12-batman-s-brisbane-an-old-lover-turns-faithless-and-its-not-the-same-anymore/) — A return visit to Brisbane reveals a city that has bulldozed its beloved old 'High Noon' pubs and Rhine-castle hotels, replaced them with brick-and-plastic horrors, and inflicted on itself a paved city square that resembles a crematorium forecourt, though Sunday drinking in the old-fashioned pubs is still going strong.
- [Please Don't Rob the Poor Man of His Beer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-06-19-batman-s-melbourne-please-dont-rob-the-poor-man-of-his-beer/) — A defence of Melbourne's drinkers ahead of a threatened Budget tax rise on beer, surveying the legal alternatives open to the conscientious objector, from home-brew kits and SOHBA lobbying to fruit wine, Zugspitze Birnenwein, and the million gallons of backyard wine made every year in Victoria.
- [Down the Paris End of Collins Street](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-06-26-batmans-melbourne-down-the-paris-end-of-collins-street/) — A lament for the demolition of the Oriental Hotel at the Paris end of Collins Street, whose bar contents sold for almost nothing at auction, and for the announcement of twin 45-storey towers to replace it, designed by I. M. Pei of New York to the indignation of Melbourne's own architects.
- [Essendon's Great Comeback in Disney Fashion](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-07-03-batman-s-melbourne-essen-dons-great-comeback-in-disney-fashion/) — Essendon Airport closes as a major domestic terminal and Melbourne shifts to Tullamarine, with Keith Dunstan reporting on the new airport's Tweedledum-and-Tweedledee symmetry between Ansett and TAA, and Reginald Ansett's grandiose 'Megacentre' redevelopment plan for the derelict 682-acre site.
- [Victoria, Bring Back the Lash](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-07-10-batmans-melbourne-victoria-bring-back-the-lash/) — Victoria remains one of the few places on earth that still has judicial flogging on its statute books, and Keith Dunstan examines the public debate after Judge Gillard and the Victorian Bar warn that courts risk being seen as too lenient on violent offenders.
- [The SF World of Bems, Sercons and BNFs](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-07-17-batman-s-melbourne-the-sf-world-of-bems-sercons-and-bnfs/) — Science fiction is experiencing its greatest boom after years of near-irrelevance, with Melbourne hosting two SF conventions in 1971, mounting a bid for the 1975 World Science Fiction Convention, and opening Australia's first dedicated SF bookshop, Space Age Books on Swanston Street, run by Mervyn Binns.
- [You Don't Have to Go to Adelaide to Be Corrupted](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-07-24-batman-s-melbourne-you-dont-have-to-go-to-adelaide-to-be-corrupted/) — Keith Dunstan argues that Melbourne's strip and nudity entertainment scene, from lunchtime shows at El Toro Espana to theatrical productions at Her Majesty's and the Chevron, can match anything Adelaide is marketing as its 'Oh! Calcutta!' coach tours, and that Melbourne's puritan reputation is undeserved.
- [Breaking Down Sexual Apartheid in a Most Endearing Way](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-07-31-batman-s-melbourne-breaking-down-sexual-apartheid-in-a-most-endearing-way/) — Geelong Grammar School headmaster T. R. Garnett announces the admission of girls from first term 1972, prompting Keith Dunstan to recall the fierce gender segregation of his own public school days and speculate on the transformation the change will bring to Corio's bleak landscape.
- [When All is Revealed There's Nothing New Left to See](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-08-07-batman-s-melbourne-when-all-is-revealed-theres-nothing-new-left-to-see/) — The annual cat-and-mouse game between General Motors-Holden and Australia's press reaches its peak with the launch of the new HQ Holden, described through elaborate factory security, undercover photography at the Dandenong plant, and the spectacular stunt of dangling the new models from BHP-ESSO helicopters over Bass Strait for a TV commercial.
- [Marriage A La Mode — Spanish, Medieval or Oz](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-08-14-batmans-melbourne-marriage-a-la-mode-spanish-medieval-or-oz/) — Melbourne's wedding reception industry is booming, with the city's new registry office installed in the Bullion Room of the old Treasury Building and Governor Rohan Delacombe opening Chaucer's, a $750,000 medieval-themed reception complex on Canterbury Road, complete with kosher kitchen, cantilever lavatories and parking for 160 cars in what the owners might reasonably call Arthur's Stables.
- [With a Tear in His Eye He Said Goodbye](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-09-18-batman-s-melbourne/) — The end of the 1971 Victorian Football League season brings the simultaneous retirement of Ron Barassi from Carlton and the resignation of Bobby Rose from Collingwood, prompting wall-to-wall press coverage and intense speculation about the coaching vacancy at Collingwood, whose traditions Keith Dunstan compares with the Japanese code of the Samurai.
- [What a Sporty Way to Govern a Country](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-09-25-batman-s-melbourne-what-a-sporty-way-to-govern-a-country/) — Exasperated by the newspaper eulogies for departing political leaders, Keith Dunstan proposes an all-sport Australian Cabinet, with Don Bradman as Prime Minister, Ron Barassi as his deputy, Ron Clarke as Treasurer, Jack Dyer handling industrial relations, Keith Miller for Transport, and Peter Thomson for National Development.
- [Whatever Is Happening to Toorak](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-10-02-batman-s-melbourne-whatever-is-happening-to-toorak/) — A lament for the decline of old Toorak, as wreckers demolish its mock Tudor streetscape to make way for a Safeway supermarket and office tower called the Village Centre.
- [A Last Fling Before Reluctant Summer Hibernation](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-10-09-batman-s-melbourne-a-last-fling-before-reluctant-summer-hibernation/) — A report on the fifth Ron Barassi Memorial Lecture at Monash University, in which Professor Ian Turner argued that Australian Rules Football is inseparable from the national character, a surrogate for warfare and a socially approved outlet for aggression.
- [Doing My Way on an Old Cigar-Box Lid](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-10-16-batman-s-melbourne-doing-my-way-on-an-old-cigar-box-lid/) — A visit to Rosalind Humphries' exhibition of paintings on cigar-box lids, which reprises a celebrated 1969 Buxton's Galleries show, while a parliamentary row over the appointment of former ASIO officer Michael Thwaites as Commonwealth Parliamentary Librarian raises questions of political discrimination in the public service.
- [Getting Away with a Gnome Even on a Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-10-23-batman-s-melbourne-getting-away-with-a-gnome-even-on-a-sunday/) — A defence of extended Sunday trading hours in Melbourne, arguing that the city's increasingly puritanical restrictions on Sunday commerce are out of step with a changing population, and that shops selling garden gnomes and concrete ornaments should be as free to open as the Dandenongs tourist trade.
- [The Bare Facts on Sexual Inflation](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-10-30-batmans-melbourne-the-bare-facts-on-sexual-inflation/) — A survey of the rising tide of sexual content in Australian newspapers, magazines and film, arguing that the market has been so flooded that the novelty has worn off, and proposing that a reformed Sex Control Board could bring some rational order to a media landscape saturated with titillation.
- [The Very Hard Week That Was](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-11-06-batmans-melbourne-the-very-hard-week-that-was/) — A report on Melbourne Wine Week, centred on a grand tasting at the Two Faces restaurant, with notes on the calibre of South Australian entries, the heroic endurance required of serious wine judges, and the state of the Australian wine industry as it faces a bottling boom from South Australia.
- [Breakfasting with the Stars, the South Yarra Push and Tails](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-11-13-batman-s-melbourne-breakfasting-with-the-stars-the-south-yarra-push-and-tails/) — A tour of the Melbourne Cup carnival season, from pre-race breakfasts at Flemington to the South Yarra social set in their tail-coats, with observations on the strange Melbourne tradition of morning champagne and the contest between formal dress and the new informality.
- [Getting Gorton Back with Kisses, Meetings and an Old Shoe Box](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-11-20-batman-s-melbourne-getting-gorton-back-with-kisses-meetings-and-an-old-shoe-box/) — A report on the grassroots Melbourne campaign to restore John Gorton to the Liberal leadership, including meetings at Malvern Town Hall, a shoe-box petition drive, and the view from a PR man that Gorton's charisma and public sympathy could yet make him Prime Minister again.
- [Now It's Hard to Be Caught with a Kids' Movie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-11-27-batmans-melbourne-now-its-hard-to-be-caught-with-a-kids-movie/) — A report on a Warner Brothers breakfast screening of a new film, where the Melbourne cinema circuit has adopted the American practice of pre-release breakfasts for press and buyers, and where the line between children's and adult films has become impossible to hold in the age of R-rated blockbusters.
- [The Triumph of Barry Mackenzie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-12-04-batman-s-melbourne-the-triumph-of-barry-mackenzie/) — Barry Humphries' comic-strip ocker hero Barry Mackenzie is being made into a film by director Phillip Adams and actor Barry Crocker, with backing from the Australian Film Development Corporation, and the production marks a turning point for an Australian film industry finally willing to celebrate its own vulgar traditions.
- [Will Howling Ruffians and Unsexed Women Threaten Melbourne Again?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-12-11-batman-s-melbourne-will-howling-ruffians-and-unsexed-women-threaten-melbourne-ag/) — The Victorian Government's moves to extend late-night shopping hours provoke a debate about the character of Melbourne's city centre after dark, drawing on Victorian-era warnings about howling ruffians and unsexed women to argue that fears about deregulated shopping hours are as overblown now as they were a century ago.
- [Innes Outback](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-12-11-innes-outback/) — A review of Hammond Innes' novel 'Outback', published by Collins, arguing that Innes has moved a long way from his early adventure-thriller formula and that the Australian outback provides him with both a vivid physical backdrop and a vehicle for examining the tensions between Aboriginal land rights and the mineral industry.
- [The Beautiful Square Dream](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1971/1971-12-18-batman-s-melbourne-the-beautiful-square-dream/) — A look at the long-delayed plans for Melbourne's City Square, surveying the proposals that have come and gone over 115 years and the latest design by the Theosophy Society, while questioning whether the square, once built, will become a genuinely beautiful civic space or merely a windy concrete plaza.
- [Feed Me Only Rhubarb Jelly](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-01-01-feed-me-only-rhubarb-jelly/) — The Weight Watchers International Christmas party at the Mayfair reception house in Elwood, where 280 members ate strictly 'legal' food, weighed to the ounce, with rhubarb jelly standing in for Christmas pudding.
- [Turn That Old Pianola](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-01-08-turn-that-old-pianola/) — An interview with Jack O'Hagan at his Elwood home on the fiftieth anniversary of 'Along the Road to Gundagai', in which he reveals he picked the town's name off a map without ever having visited the place.
- [Pioneering at $50 a Day](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-02-05-pioneering-at-50-a-day/) — A visit to Naringal, a stately homestead near Ballarat run by the Rowe family for American tourists, offering colonial pastoral life complete with silver candelabra, kangaroo-spotting, and a tour of the family cemetery.
- [Home Brewers Take the Field](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-02-12-home-brewers-take-the-field/) — The home brewing boom that swept Melbourne following Carlton brewery's public objections to amateur beer-making in 1971, with fermenters filling refrigerators and the Olinda kit-maker reporting growth of several hundred percent.
- [Random Notes of a Citizen in Gloom](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-02-19-random-notes-of-a-citizen-in-gloom/) — Melbourne's SEC power strike of February 1972, observed from the premiere of a new Australian play in darkness to Sir Henry Bolte backing winners at the Pakenham Races while the city's air conditioners and swimming pools sat idle.
- [The Jeanagers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-02-19-the-jeanagers/) — A visit to Jean City, the new jeans shop in Swanston Street, Melbourne, where Carlton brewery beer-label T-shirts sit alongside Wrangler and Levis, and proprietor David Anderson's philosophy is that anything too fancy would drive customers straight back to Myers.
- [Regressors, It's Time to March](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-02-26-regressors-its-time-to-march/) — The closure of the Federal Hotel in Collins Street, Melbourne, an 1888 Coffee Palace of sculptured Victorian excess, prompts a call for a Society Against Progress to resist the city's unstoppable appetite for demolition.
- [A Grand Vision for Melbourne](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-03-04-a-grand-vision-for-melbourne/) — The launch of the Flinders Gate project, a plan to redevelop Melbourne's Flinders Street railway yards into hotels, cinemas and a new station, with the name 'Flinders Gate' winning a public competition after readers submitted suggestions ranging from Ned's Nook to Squizzy's Place.
- [Tourists Adore This Horror](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-03-11-tourists-adore-this-horror/) — The irony of Melbourne's two jails in 1972, with the old Russell Street Gaol opened to tourists by the National Trust while Pentridge in Coburg makes the news for prisoner riots and conditions John Galbally called an affront to human dignity.
- [Whatever Happened to the Old Cricket Fury?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-03-18-whatever-happened-to-the-old-cricket-fury/) — A historical survey of passionate cricket fan protests over selection decisions, arguing that the fury sparked by Bill Lawry's axing from the Australian touring team in 1972 is mild compared with the monster indignation meetings, brawling selectors, and prisoner protests of earlier eras.
- [The Siege of Rutherglen](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-03-25-the-siege-of-rutherglen/) — The Labor Day weekend Rutherglen Wine Festival, when between 15,000 and 20,000 young people descended on the small Victorian wine town of 1200 residents for three days of mass public drinking and police with paddy wagons.
- [Take Me to Your Folk Museum!](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-04-01-take-me-to-your-folk-museum/) — The heritage tourism boom sweeping Victoria's country towns, from Echuca's paddlesteamer wharf to Ballarat's Sovereign Hill, as local councils discover that history and nostalgia make marvellous motel-fillers.
- [How Groceries Went Foreign](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-04-08-how-groceries-went-foreign/) — Jim Cairns' warning that foreign interests would control half of Australian manufacturing within a decade, illustrated by a walk around a local supermarket where almost nothing from cornflakes to pet food is still Australian-owned.
- [A Lovely War at the Werribee Gorge](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-04-15-a-lovely-war-at-the-werribee-gorge/) — Australian units of American Civil War re-enactors camp for four days at the Werribee Gorge near Bacchus Marsh, with muzzle loaders, Confederate uniforms, a Union loyalist doomed to die at every outing, and evidence of Foster's Lager burned black in the campfire.
- [A New Religion for Winter](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-04-22-a-new-religion-for-winter/) — Melbourne's devotion to Australian Rules football described as a full-blown religion, from a widow's request to inter her husband's ashes in Richmond's goal square to the Victorian government's approval of VFL Football Pools and the imminent launch of Tattslotto.
- [Barking About a Bite](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-05-06-barking-about-a-bite/) — Uncle Ben's launches its new Pal Meaty Bites dog food at the Old Melbourne Motor Inn with a fashion parade inside a giant inflatable dog, a Cinemascope interview, and a banquet for 80 grocery executives and their wives flown in from around Australia.
- [Feathering the Top Eagle's Pad](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-05-20-feathering-the-top-eagles-pad/) — Melbourne's new wave of luxury city apartment towers, from Michael Edgley's penthouse at Park Towers in Spring Street to the $250,000 24th-floor suite at 99 Spring Street with marble from Greece and tiles from Italy, and the more modest 135-flat Lonsdale Heights for those who prefer their galvanised iron roof-top views.
- [Graduates of the Money Game](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-06-17-graduates-of-the-money-game/) — A chemistry graduate turned cab driver, one of 14 unemployed out of 18 in his cohort, prompts a proposal for a 'Bachelor of Materialism' degree, with George Frew, Bruce Small, David Wynn and Norman Shierlaw as lecturers, Sir Reginald Ansett as dean, and Sir Henry Bolte conferring degrees.
- [The Winter of Their Discontent](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-06-24-the-winter-of-their-discontent/) — Melbourne's warm and snowless June of 1972 leaves ski-resort operators nursing heavy losses, while Keith Dunstan reports from Falls Creek on the fashion designer lodges, ski-gear merchants and the Thai-roofed retreat of the city's 'Duckfeather king.'
- [The Playing Fields of Oakleigh Motel](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-07-01-the-playing-fields-of-oakleigh-motel/) — A visit to the Victorian War Games Association's re-enactment of the Battle of Waterloo, staged with thousands of model soldiers at the Oakleigh Motel, where Napoleon was played by the restaurant manager and Wellington by an excitable computer programmer.
- [Stooping to the Sin of Judas](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-07-08-stooping-to-the-sin-of-judas/) — Victoria's expansion of legalised gambling from Tattersalls to Tattslotto and football pools prompts a survey of the clergy's silence compared to their outrage in 1953, and a tongue-in-cheek call for a transport lottery to cover the railways' $36 million annual loss.
- [The City That Lost Its Taste](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-07-15-the-city-that-lost-its-taste/) — A visit to Brisbane's rapidly modernising cityscape prompts regret for lost cast-iron pubs, demolished heritage buildings and the cancelled potential of an Australian New Orleans, while still finding warmth in the sunshine and the avocadoes.
- [Shadows on the Sunshine Coast](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-07-22-shadows-on-the-sunshine-coast/) — A visit to the Gold Coast during the Winter Bowls Carnival finds mayor Bruce Small championing $99 package tours to offset cyclone damage and lost tourists, while the construction of a 17-storey beachfront tower sparks a protest campaign over shadows, erosion and the relentless ugliness of outdoor advertising.
- [Dolls Without Cutters](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-07-29-dolls-without-cutters/) — A visit to Cairns during the cane-burning season finds the cane-cutters replaced by machines, a city whose temperatures are close to perfection despite wet-season toads and burning-cane ash in swimming pools, and novelist Xavier Herbert working in a bush house on a 500,000-word novel he describes as his reason for being on earth.
- [Sporting Bad Relations](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-08-05-sporting-bad-relations/) — On the eve of the Munich Olympics, an accumulation of incidents from cricket and rugby suggests Australian sporting teams are building a reputation for bad behaviour, prompting the proposal for a goodwill ship tour of Asia whose teams would always contrive to lose.
- [Bazza Arrives on the Silver Screen](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-08-19-bazza-arrives-on-the-silver-screen/) — A preview of the forthcoming film "The Adventures of Barry McKenzie" at Sydney University finds Barry Crocker as a lovable ocker innocent amid rapacious Poms, complete with a chunder song, a colour chunder scene, and a supporting cast including Spike Milligan, Peter Cook and Dennis Price.
- [Bolte — The last of the Victorians](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-08-19-bolte-the-last-of-the-victorians/) — A profile of Henry Bolte on his retirement after 17 years as Victorian premier, arguing through assessments from Clyde Holding and Jim McDonald that Bolte's rough, anti-intellectual self-certainty was both his greatest political skill and a perfect mirror for the city he ruled.
- [Taking the Bite out of Shark](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-08-26-taking-the-bite-out-of-shark/) — Victoria's ban on school shark over 28 inches for food, prompted by mercury contamination, threatens to devastate the fish and chip industry whose 24 million pieces of "flake" a year represent 70 per cent of Victorian fish consumption, and prompts speculation about what to call the shark should it need a new name.
- [Evolving the Mayoral Egg](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-09-09-evolving-the-mayoral-egg/) — An examination of Melbourne's arcane system for electing its lord mayor through the Civic Group's private Sunday-night caucus, prompted by the first-ever dropping of an incumbent after one term and the quiet elevation of a former RAAF fighter pilot in his place.
- [Sock It to Me, Pharaoh!](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-09-16-sock-it-to-me-pharaoh/) — A report on St Paul's Cathedral's rock opera season in which Russell Morris performed 'Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat', Johnny Farnham starred as the Prodigal Son and Colleen Hewett followed in 'David and a Golden Throne', all to packed houses amid protests outside.
- [Grease Up to Your Ducktail Hairdo](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-09-23-grease-up-to-your-ducktail-hairdo/) — A report on Harry Miller's production of 'Grease' at the Metro Theatre and its fancy-dress first night, with reflections on Melbourne's nostalgia obsession and the observation that the city is still so far behind the 1950s it barely needs to reach backwards.
- [It's Been a Very Hard Month](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-09-30-its-been-a-very-hard-month/) — A report on the five major banquets and three club dinners marking Henry Bolte's retirement, culminating in the 1,200-person Liberal Party dinner at the Royal Ballroom, with a selection of the premier's most quotable farewell remarks.
- [Turn-Up for an Old Style](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-10-07-turn-up-for-an-old-style/) — A column on the return of trouser turn-ups, enormous lapels and high heels to men's fashion, prompted by the visit of London designer Hardy Amies, with statistics showing Australian men spend only $32 a year on clothing.
- [It's All in the Rules](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-10-14-its-all-in-the-rules/) — A Grand Final week report covering Cyril Pearl's symbolic football burning outside the MCG, the Anti-Football League selling 60,000 non-seats, and the Ron Barassi Sixth Memorial Lecture at Monash University, in which the football-as-sex-act thesis was proved to thunderous applause.
- [Outracing the Race of the Year](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-10-21-outracing-the-race-of-the-year/) — A report on the Ocean Racing Club of Victoria's new Melbourne-to-Hobart yacht race, launching on Boxing Day in direct competition with the Sydney-Hobart, with a defence of Victoria's deeper ocean racing tradition.
- [Public Snoop into Private Domain](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-10-28-public-snoop-into-private-domain/) — A tour of Melbourne's post-football display home season, cataloguing the year's fashion for Spanish-style brick arches and adobe, the proliferation of royal and explorer names, and the deep psychological satisfaction of snooping through someone else's house for free.
- [The Most Honorable Sport](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-11-04-the-most-honorable-sport/) — A review of R. S. Whitington's illustrated history of Australian cricket, tracing the game's Golden Age from the 1890s to 1912 through Trumper, Macartney and Ranjitsinhji, and noting the book's peculiar distinction of two prestigious forewords and no index.
- [Masterpiece or Failure](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-11-11-masterpiece-or-failure/) — A report on the National Gallery's purchase of Jean-Robert Ipousteguy's 'La Mort du Pere' for $60,000, in which Patrick McCaughey called it 'bloody silly', Eric Westbrook called it 'absolutely stunning', Fred Williams said it was 'all a bit bloody queer', and an anonymous Melbourne Revolutionary Surrealist Society donated a rival sculpture on a bullock dray.
- [Manning the Ramparts](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-11-18-manning-the-ramparts/) — A defence of the Windsor Hotel against the threat of redevelopment, tracing its history from the 1886 temperance grand opening, when James Munro burned the liquor licence, through 1920 reinstatement, to its status as Melbourne's last great hotel with atmosphere.
- [The Majesty of World Golf](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-11-25-the-majesty-of-world-golf/) — A report from the World Cup contest at Royal Melbourne Golf Club, where Bruce Crampton's agonisingly methodical putting was contrasted with Roberto de Vicenzo's joyful, chatty approach to the game, while running like Herb Elliott was required to stay close to any gallery.
- [On Holey Ground](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-12-02-on-holey-ground/) — A tribute to Melbourne's hole-watching tradition, tracing the city's rivalry with Sydney's famous Chevron 'Golden Hole', celebrating the new 60-foot Mainline Corporation dig at the Collins Street end, and noting that Whelan the Wrecker's demolition of a whole block has finally given Melbourne a hole worth admiring.
- [Doing a Biggles](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-12-09-doing-a-biggies/) — A report on the RAAF Flying Club's two-day Tiger Moth fly-in at Point Cook, where 12 of the expected 21 vintage biplanes assembled for a formation fly-past, their owners as passionate about original detail as veteran car men, and the whole squadron barely moving against a strong Geelong Road headwind.
- [Nureyev Observed](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-12-16-nureyev-observed/) — A behind-the-scenes visit to the filming of Nureyev's 'Don Quixote' at Essendon airport hangars, where Sir Robert Helpmann lay in a vast four-poster bed, Ray Powell endured 12 hours sewn into a Sancho Panza costume, and Nureyev himself, in purple polo-neck, woollen trousers and a balaclava in 90-degree heat, never once stopped moving.
- [Send Back a Christmas Card Today](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1972/1972-12-30-send-back-a-christmas-card-today/) — A ruthless knocking attack on the commercial Christmas machine, tracing the year's selling seasons from January sales through Mother's Day to Cup Week, announcing the formation of the Scrooge Society of Australia to abolish Christmas altogether, and rehabilitating Ebenezer Scrooge as a visionary done in by bad public relations.
- [Horsetrader Henry](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-01-06-books-horsetrader-henry/) — A review of Peter Blazey's political biography of Henry Bolte, noting the dearth of Victorian state political biography and assessing Blazey's account of the premier's press management strategy, his brusqueness in cabinet, and the agony surrounding the hanging of Ronald Ryan.
- [Advice for the new team](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-01-06-outand-about-with-batman-advice-for-the-new-team/) — A satirical manifesto of advice to the newly elected Whitlam government, proposing new ministries for quality of life, gambling, sex, sport and protests, with nominations for permanent heads including George Moore, Germaine Greer and Barry Humphries.
- [A sport of our own](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-01-13-out-and-about-with-batman-a-sport-of-our-own/) — A report from the World Rabbit Skinning Championship at Moyston in the Victorian Grampians, where Keith Dunstan witnesses champion shearer Ron Crawford lose his crown to local farmer Eddie Overington, and argues the event deserves Olympic recognition alongside watermelon pip spitting.
- [The horror game](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-01-20-out-and-about-with-batman-the-horror-game/) — A visit to the former Melbourne Gaol after its transfer to the National Trust, where new displays of death masks, four skulls including Ned Kelly's, and the execution platform have elevated Melbourne's horror tourism above the Tower of London, though the authenticity of the Kelly skull remains disputed.
- [Cobber dobbers in Sunstroke Strip](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-01-27-out-and-about-with-batman-cobber-dobbers-in-sunstroke-strip/) — Melbourne's second water crisis in five years has produced a new community phenomenon, the neighbour who rats on illegal waterers, garden bore-sinking at $1200 a pop, and a booming trade in plastic buckets and rubber bath-water diverters, prompting Keith Dunstan to suggest the city rebrand as Sunstroke Strip.
- [Sacrilegious identity crisis](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-02-24-out-and-about-sacrilegious-identity-crisis/) — The VFL's new ten-year rule allowing veteran players to transfer freely has caused Melbourne a collective mental breakdown, with icons like Doug Wade going to North Melbourne, Carl Ditterich sold to Melbourne for $82,000, and Ron Barassi transferred to Carlton, destroying the tribal suburban loyalties that gave football its passionate meaning.
- [The big statue wrap-up](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-03-10-out-and-about-with-batman-the-big-statue-wrap-up/) — Inspired by Max Beerbohm's idea of covering London's statues rather than unveiling new ones, Keith Dunstan proposes a programme of veiling ceremonies for Sydney's pompous colonial bronzes, beginning with the dumpy Queen Victoria near the Supreme Court and moving on to Captain Cook, Captain Arthur Phillip and the weather-checking King Edward VII.
- [Initiation into the wine cult](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-03-24-out-and-about-with-batman-initiation-into-the-wine-cult/) — Keith Dunstan attends two landmark first-vintage dinners in the Hunter Valley, visiting the ultra-modern automated winery at Hollydene near Muswellbrook and Rothbury's ecclesiastical great hall, where he receives a low pass in his grape-identification test and Len Evans advises him to drink harder.
- [Southerner in Sydney](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-03-31-out-and-about-with-batman-southerner-in-sydney/) — A Melbourne journalist's two weeks in Sydney yields observations on the city's omnipresent navel, its spectacular rainfall, the death of Kings Cross's sinful reputation, and the replacement of old-style pubs with pseudo-Tudor beamed interiors, plus a homesick longing for the clop of milk-cart horses on Toorak bitumen.
- [If marriage were abolished](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-04-14-out-and-about-with-batman-if-marriage-were-abolished/) — The Whitlam government's proposed divorce reforms prompt Keith Dunstan to calculate the social and economic consequences of marriage's abolition, from confused dinner party seating and turbulent social pages through to the collapse of the wedding photography and reception industry and the ruin of jewellers.
- [Through a tramcar window](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-04-21-out-and-about-with-batman-through-a-tramcar-window/) — The Metropolitan Tramways Board's plan to replace Melbourne's beloved old trams with 100 smooth, silent modern vehicles alarms Keith Dunstan, who proposes instead to have Ronald Searle or Bruce Petty design a nostalgic cast-iron beauty, with tourist trams running to Toorak and St Kilda complete with velvet seats and mahogany bars.
- [Sliding into corruption](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-05-05-out-and-about-with-batman-sliding-into-corruption/) — A formerly clean-minded journalist surveys his local newsagent's paperback rack, finds 197 of 300 covers show bared women, reads a Number 96 tie-in novel's breathless prose, and concludes that sex has killed off the wholesome Western, and that only cleverly promoted immorality in Westerns could save it.
- [Glories of the site office](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-05-12-out-and-about-with-batman-glories-of-the-site-office/) — The twin-tower Collins Place project in Melbourne has built a $140,000 architect's site office so magnificent, with cathedral archways, 32 offices, PABX switchboards and pocket radios, that Keith Dunstan argues the city should forget the towers and simply lease the offices at $10 a square foot.
- [Too late into nostalgia](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-05-19-out-and-about-with-batman-too-late-into-nostalgia/) — Keith Dunstan's five-year-old business plan for Batman Atmosphere Laboratories, to mass-produce antique-look decor items from Greek columns to plastic cast-iron lacework, has been comprehensively beaten to market, with firms already selling machine-made antique bricks, fibreglass castles and miniature Waterloo cannons at $500 apiece.
- [Up there, Cazaly (10 points daily)](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-05-26-out-and-about-with-batman-up-there-cazaly-10-points-daily/) — The Broadcasting Control Board's new Australian content points system throws an imagined commercial TV station into crisis, as its executives frantically try to squeeze poetry, literary criticism and ballet out of 81 hours of weekly football coverage, eventually hitting on a David Williamson sex-and-football drama combining 'Number 96' with the MCG.
- [The delights of federatus interuptus](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-06-02-out-and-about-with-batman-the-delights-of-federatus-interuptus/) — Keith Dunstan proposes that Australia's restless states capitalise on Queensland's secession agitation by de-federating on May 9, 1974 or 1975 with all the pomp of the 1901 Federation opening in Melbourne, complete with marching girls, six separate national anthems and Queensland's military likely taking over Government House.
- [We're all so delighted, obviously](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-06-09-out-and-about-with-batman-we-re-all-so-delighted-obviously/) — Princess Anne's engagement to Lieutenant Mark Phillips revives Keith Dunstan's memories of covering Princess Margaret's engagement in 1960, when every newspaper deployed the word "obviously" to imagine royal feelings, Collins Street jewellers had replica engagement rings on display within days, and correspondents speculated the honeymoon must obviously be in Australia.
- [Full steam ahead for GM-H boss](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-06-16-out-and-about-with-batman-full-steam-ahead-for-gm-h-boss/) — Bill Gibbs, managing director of General Motors-Holden and new chairman of the loss-making Victorian Railways, should take a lesson from Echuca, where the annual steam and traction rally assembles entire squadrons of vintage Fowler steam engines, a steam pipe-organ and an eight-ton 1924 Sentinel steam truck whose party trick is tipping in three directions.
- [Colour blind to the grim facts](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-06-23-out-and-about-with-batman-color-blind-to-the-grim-facts/) — Melbourne's commercial dream of selling objects in football club colours always fails, from Gas and Fuel Corporation porcelain stoves in all 12 club colours to Myers' wash-and-wear synthetic wigs at $6.50, while Keith Dunstan's 43-year survey of attendance figures reveals VFL crowds have fallen from nine percent of Melbourne's population in 1930 to only 5.3 percent today.
- [Suffocated by awful anthems](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-06-30-out-and-about-with-batman-suffocated-by-awful-anthems/) — Whitlam's national anthem competition produces terrible entries dominated by the words "God save," "Gough," and odes to nickel mines, but Keith Dunstan argues the best solution is to make Australia unique as the one country in the world that inflicts no national anthem on its subjects, since making 'Waltzing Matilda' official would ruin it forever.
- [Tasmanian sin needs a fair go](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-07-07-out-and-about-with-batman-tasmanian-sin-needs-a-fair-go/) — Every time Tasmania pioneers a decently sinful enterprise, the other states steal it, from the Tattersalls lottery to off-course betting to 10 o'clock closing, and now Wrest Point is offering Australia's first legal two-up but hesitating over who to appoint as ringmaster, while New South Wales threatens to legalise gambling houses and claim the sin capital mantle.
- [What we need is a virile virus](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-07-14-out-and-about-with-batman-what-we-need-is-a-virile-virus/) — A survey of 17 years of newspaper virus vogues reveals a progression from Asian flu to Echo 6, American flu, Russian flu, Hong Kong flu and now London flu, and Keith Dunstan proposes that Australia should stake its own claim on the 1974 flu season by naming it the Whitlam grippe, boosting the prime minister's international profile while capitalising on 19th-century nostalgia.
- [Now it's back to square one](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-07-21-out-and-about-with-batman-now-it-s-back-to-square-one/) — Melbourne's decades-long city square saga returns to its starting point when English finance company Star Holdings collapses with over a million dollars in losses, meaning the Regent Theatre need never have closed, Hilliers' chocolate shop need never have shut, and the battle to save the Regent is on again, prompted by a letter from Barry Humphries of Canterbury.
