- [Eata bitta breada day](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-07-28-out-and-about-with-batman-eata-bitta-breada-day/) — Amid the great diet bore of 1973, with 235 household diets in two years and Henry Bolte's grapefruit causing an Israeli fortune, the bread manufacturers fight back with a six-slices-a-day diet launched in the rain at Caulfield railway station with Ron Barassi present, though Keith Dunstan suggests the real PR solution would be spreading a rumour that wholemeal bread is the most potent aphrodisiac known to mankind.
- [A boat trip into the past](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-08-04-out-and-about-with-batman-a-boat-trip-into-the-past/) — Echuca's purchase of the 1906 paddle steamer Pevensey from a reluctant Mildura for $20,000 brings Keith Dunstan aboard as a crew member for the voyage up the Murray, moving at a 19th-century pace of 3 mph among pelicans and black swans, with a 65-year-old skipper born on a river boat who learned that on a river boat you have a front and a back, never port and starboard.
- [Rubbishing the brochure fiends](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-08-11-out-and-about-with-batman-rubbishing-the-brochure-fiends/) — Keith Dunstan proposes a Cram device, a combination rubbish bin and letterbox with a ball-bearing swivel allowing one swift flick to tip the entire morning's mail into the rubbish, as a remedy for the flood of direct mail targeting newly engaged, newly expecting and house-building households with everything from medieval-themed wedding menus to bronze-dipped baby booties.
- [Captain Cook's cottage in sad decline](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-08-18-captain-cook-s-cottage-in-sad-decline/) — Melbourne's Captain Cook's Cottage, acquired in 1933 when philanthropist Russell Grimwade bought and shipped the Yorkshire house to Fitzroy Gardens, has risen from third to possibly first among the city's tourist attractions in the nostalgia wave, but The Age has now reported grimy walls, a leaking roof and water-drenched furniture, leaving the cottage due for a complete updating.
- [Cashing in on Kelly](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-08-18-out-and-about-with-batman-cashing-in-on-kelly/) — Glenrowan, long notorious for turning its back on its most famous son, has been transformed by Don and Valda Tibbits's Glenrowan Tourist Centre into a Kelly shrine with a giant fibreglass figure on the roof, while visitors can buy Ned Kelly T-shirts, beer mugs, tea towels and candles, and the star exhibit is Mick Jagger's fibreglass armour from the Kelly film.
- [A new weapon in the beer war](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-08-25-out-and-about-with-batman-a-new-weapon-in-the-beer-war/) — Courage Brewery's latest gambit in its disappointing campaign against Carlton is to put Brownlow Medal contenders' faces on aluminium cans, but after $5 million in accumulated losses and a series of failed products from Crest to Colonial Ale to Tankard beer, Keith Dunstan suggests they would do better decorating cans with writers, since almost all great Australian writers drink awfully well.
- [Wrest Point isn't Tasmania's costliest joint](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-09-01-out-and-about-with-batman-wrest-point-isn-t-tasmania-s-costliest-joint/) — Hawthorn's desperate and expensive pursuit of returning full forward Peter Hudson, who damaged his knee playing against Melbourne a year ago and has been the subject of front-page leads and middle-page spreads ever since, prompts Keith Dunstan to call for an Anti-Cartilage Council and a Chair of Cartiology at the University of Melbourne, since if a club is buying a player for $60,000 it would be fair to ask that he come pre-operated.
- [The mouse that roared](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-09-08-out-and-about-with-batman-the-mouse-that-roared/) — Disney World ambassador Frank describes to Keith Dunstan how Walt Disney secretly bought 43 square miles of Florida under assumed names, built a 1057-room hotel with a monorail running into its fourth floor, and now attracts 12 million visitors a year, while a Japanese former prisoner of war on a pilgrimage to see Phar Lap's stuffed hide provides the funniest sight Frank has seen at Disney World.
- [A man as tall as a telegraph pole](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-09-15-out-and-about-a-man-as-tall-as-a-telegraph-pole/) — David Williamson returns from London after The Removalists' West End run, surprised by critics who called it evil, revolting and unsuitable for Australian tourists, while Harry M. Miller's 60-foot sign outside the Royal Court Theatre confirms the classic Australian principle that you must win distinction overseas before Australians will admit you are any good.
- [Get rid of that (beep) telephone](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-09-22-out-and-about-get-rid-of-that-beep-telephone/) — The PMG's new 50-mile range paging device prompts Keith Dunstan to declare a pox on the telephone and report with admiration on Gordon De'Lisle, the Melbourne businessman who retired to Buderim, Queensland and refused to have a telephone installed even when the PMG sent in a team and his refusal caused them to be stunned beyond belief.
- [Last of the great footy finals](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-09-29-cover-story-last-of-the-great-footy-finals/) — With the VFL's contract with the MCG expired, the question is whether the grand final will eventually move to Waverley Park, which opened in 1970 and will hold 80,000 by next year but can only be reached by car through catastrophic traffic jams, while the MCG remains one of the five biggest grounds in the world and the only place where a human being can have the opportunity of being hooted by 120,000.
- [Melbourne v. Sydney: The Love-Hate Feud](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/readers-digest/1973/melbourne-v-sydney-the-love-hate-feud/) — A Melbourne man's affectionate account of the long civic rivalry between Melbourne and Sydney, from Parliament's original seat in Melbourne to the competing airports, opera houses and sporting loyalties that kept the two cities in a state of permanent, mostly enjoyable mutual suspicion.
- [Not a pigmy lady in sight](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-10-06-batmans-melbourne-not-a-pigmy-lady-in-sight/) — Tom Wittingslow, who has attended 41 Melbourne Shows with 40 rides, side-shows and 180 employees, laments that the sideshow has been killed off by strip clubs, TV boxing money and leagues clubs, leaving only a Siamese twins illusion done by mirrors and his prize new Turbo ride, a $180,000 double ferris wheel designed to create maximum discomfort and inspire the greatest terror.
- [Toward a more viable tax scene](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-10-13-toward-a-more-viable-tax-scene/) — Treasurer Crean's inflation problem could be solved by a cliche tax ranging from $50 for the return of "churching the old whore" to 25 cents for each "in fact," since Keith Dunstan's monitoring of Parliament and TV current affairs reveals an epidemic of "viable," "cogent," "in this area," "gut feeling" and the coming word "elan," with Senator Gair's "fleas on an old dog" worth another $50.
- [From Rolls-Royce to push bike](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-10-27-batmans-melbourne-from-rolls-royce-to-push-bike/) — Melbourne's 4000-strong Pedal for Paths rally along Alexandra Avenue features a gentleman arriving in a Rolls-Royce who opens the boot, assembles a folding English bike and pedals off amidst cheers, an 81-year-old on a wooden leg, a former world cycling champion now 40 pounds heavier, and a Ferntree Gully man's Taiwanese pedicab whose passengers must dismount at every hill.
- [Fashion gets it in the neck](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-11-03-batmans-melbourne-fashion-gets-it-in-the-neck/) — Attending the Sydney Opera House opening in an outdated suit, Keith Dunstan consults Melbourne fashion designer Mike Treloar, who reports that ties are dying except for enormous Oscar Wilde bow ties, open-necked shirts are the new look and chest hair is the status symbol, while Italian tie-maker Ottavio Ermini arrives to argue that the tie is the key of a man's personality and the Japanese will pay anything for a Gallieni pure silk spinnaker.
- [Concern over a noble pub](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-11-10-batmans-melbourne-concern-over-a-noble-pub/) — Melbourne's last noble old hotel, the Windsor, faces a Commodore Group takeover bid at $2.30 a share, prompting Keith Dunstan to recall its founding as a temperance coffee palace in 1884 and the grand moment when Hon James Munro burned its liquor licence, then to speculate that its location opposite Parliament House and near the Reserve Bank and two churches would make it ideal for conversion to a casino.
- [Getting a visa for Ayers Rock](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-11-17-batmans-melbourne-getting-a-visa-for-ayers-rock/) — A House of Representatives committee's recommendation to restrict tourist access to Ayers Rock as a national heritage area would create the world's first example of tourist rationing, prompting Keith Dunstan to propose relieving the pressure by turning Hobart into a free port, building a Bibleland near Alice Springs, and appointing an anti-tourist officer to restrict access to Phar Lap, Chloe and Ned Kelly's skull.
- [The heart of the matter](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-11-24-batmans-melbourne-the-heart-of-the-matter/) — The year's contradictory medical advice on heart health has Keith Dunstan hopelessly confused, as sugar, coffee, salt, jogging, fast driving, budgerigars, bottle-fed infancy and working all threaten cardiac arrest, while three to six drinks a day, church attendance, married sex and eating like an Eskimo offer protection, with a Danish dentist recommending removing all teeth early as the safest precaution of all.
- [Rolling down to Wodonga](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-12-01-batmans-melbourne-rolling-down-to-wodonga/) — Bill Gibbs, new chairman of the Victorian Railways, tours the system in his personal locomotive driven by 20-stone champion steak-eater Les Haining, unveils a plaque at Glenrowan commemorating Ned Kelly's forced removal of the railway tracks and leads a cavalcade to the Wodonga centenary, where the 1873 border celebrations were marred by rival states fighting over whose bread should top the sandwiches.
- [Bubbling over with enthusiasm](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-12-08-batmans-melbourne-bubbling-over-with-enthusiasm/) — Seppelts Great Western opens its first on-site liquor store with an air-conditioned Mercedes bus from Melbourne and champagne flowing from 10.15 am, as Keith Dunstan explores the 1865 gold-miners' underground drives now crammed with two million bottles and meets Jack Floyd, chief shaker for 30 years, who jiggles 25,000 bottles a day to settle the deposit onto the cork.
- [Ear-bashers' annual orgy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1973/1973-12-15-batmans-melbourne-ear-bashers-annual-orgy/) — Melbourne's school speech nights, unchanged in pattern since Keith Dunstan first attended 45 years ago, follow an invariable formula of Gilbert and Sullivan, the headmaster's report on school finances, a visiting dignitary who has been booked as guest speaker at every school at the same time, and speeches so excruciating that one is left wondering why there have been campaigns for the abolition of examinations but none for the abolition of school speech nights.
- [Footballers get worker power](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-01-05-batmans-melbourne-footballers-get-worker-power/) — The formation of the Victorian Football League Players' Association at a secret meeting at Melbourne University's Union House prompts Keith Dunstan to imagine the consequences of a footballers' union capable of black banning finals and stopping the game.
- [Fun and gore on the Bazza set](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-01-12-batman-at-paim-beach-fun-and-gore-on-the-bazza-set/) — Keith Dunstan watches the first day of filming of 'Barry McKenzie Holds His Own' at Palm Beach, where director Bruce Beresford orchestrates scores of blood-drenched extras and an imported CSIRO blowfly to create scenes of carnage on the beach and an idyllic barbecue beside Pittwater.
- [Oh to be in Australia now that Al's there](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-01-19-batmans-melbourne-oh-to-be-in-australia-now-that-al-s-there/) — Al Grassby's push to attract 250,000 expatriate Australians home inspires Keith Dunstan to propose a network of Australian Nostalgia Centres in London, Paris and New York, stocked with Fosters, Four 'n' Twenty pies, footy replays and Violet Crumble Bars.
- [Anyone in need of a silver elephant howdah?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-02-16-batmans-melbourne-anyone-in-need-of-a-silver-elephant-howdah/) — Melbourne antique dealers Ed Clark and Jim Elder gamble $25,000 in transport costs to bring 19 maharajah's coaches, 30 chandeliers and four elephant howdahs from the palace of the Maharajah of Mysore to the Malvern Town Hall for auction.
- [A lot of fun and games](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-02-23-batmans-melbourne-a-lot-of-fun-and-games/) — A new Monopoly set for the holidays prompts Keith Dunstan to survey the booming market for topical board games, from Squatter and Watergate to imagined future games about the petrol crisis, corrupt doctors, Black Power and Australian bank robbers on the run in Rio.
- [On the outer in underwear](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-03-02-batmans-melbourne-on-the-outer-in-underwear/) — A birthday gift of expensive French black underpants sends Keith Dunstan into a Collins Street men's wear shop to discover that underwear has become a fashion statement, with designs from French girls in outline to spider motifs, zodiac signs and padded novelty items.
- [At Ripponlea it's all over bar the sightseeing](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-03-09-batmans-melbourne-at-ripponlea-it-s-all-over-bar-the-sightseeing/) — After 11 years of legal battles between the National Trust and the Commonwealth over Ripponlea estate in Elsternwick, the mansion and its 13 acres of Guilfoyle-designed gardens are finally open to the public, drawing crowds that produced a traffic jam half a mile long on the first weekend.
- [Cars that dreams are made of](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-03-16-batmans-melbourne-cars-that-dreams-are-made-of/) — The Melbourne Motor Show at the Exhibition Building showcases Maserati, Ferrari, Lamborghini, Aston Martin and De Tomaso alongside a Range Rover, a Leyland floating in dry ice and an experimental safety Toyota, all priced from $19,000 to $55,000, and not one person mentions the energy crisis.
- [A vineyard to end all vineyards](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-03-23-batmans-melbourne-a-vineyard-to-end-all-vineyards/) — The grand opening of the Mitchelton winery on the Goulburn River near Nagambie reveals a $3.5 million operation with nine radio-equipped hostesses, three licensed restaurants, a 200-foot tower, an aviary, a swimming pool, a chapel and a supermarket-style tasting room designed to process 1000 visitors a day.
- [A long love affair with a DC3](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-03-30-batmans-melbourne-a-long-love-affair-with-a-dc3/) — Ansett's nostalgia flights by DC3, the same aircraft Keith Dunstan's father took him to see at Essendon Airport in 1938, reunite British comedian Jimmy Edwards with the plane he flew on D-Day and survived being shot down over Holland, and the comedian gives the tyre a hefty kick for old times' sake.
- [How to launch a custard pie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-04-06-batmans-melbourne-how-to-launch-a-custard-pie/) — Pie-throwing at the Prime Minister during the Western Australian election campaign revives Keith Dunstan's interest in the history and technique of custard pie projection, with guidance from Mack Sennett's memoirs and Barry Humphries on why shaving cream beats actual custard for television.
- [Mainly froth and bubbles](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-04-27-batmans-melbourne-mainly-froth-and-bubbles/) — New laws banning the word 'champagne' from Australian fizzy wine have spawned a remarkable range of substitutes, Champers, Champeaux, Champearl, Chalet Blue Rhapsody, Cold Duck, Sparkling Sangria and Sparkling Spumante, prompting Keith Dunstan to survey the fizz capital of the world.
- [Democracy in denim pants](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-05-04-batmans-melbourne-democracy-in-denim-pants/) — A worldwide shortage of denim, the fabric that the magazine 'Clothes' says has united capitalist and communist, Arab and Jew, brings Keith Dunstan to Yakka's sales manager and Melbourne's swing-door jeaneries, where 15 million pairs were sold in Australia in 1973.
- [Streaking bad for business](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-05-11-batmans-melbourne-streaking-bad-for-business/) — With 328 streaking cases since February, including a Mercedes-driving department-store manager who water-skied naked down the Yarra, Keith Dunstan surveys the threat streaking poses to the massage parlour, photography, strip club, newspaper and hotel industries that have built their entire business model on the rarity of nudity.
- [Room to learn at the top](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-05-18-batmans-melbourne-room-to-learn-at-the-top/) — A Jones, Lang and Wootton review reveals 11 per cent of Melbourne's office space stands empty, 1.7 million square feet by year's end, prompting Keith Dunstan to propose turning the city's prestige towers, including the 50-storey Nauru House and the twin 40-storey Collins Place towers, into schools with panoramic views and wall-to-wall carpet.
- [The boss is busy in room 350](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-05-25-batmans-melbourne-the-boss-is-busy-in-room-350/) — A three-week hotel workers' strike, rejected a $14-a-week rise in favour of $20, forces hotel owners and managers across Melbourne to make beds, wash dishes and work the bars themselves, including the Windsor Hotel's manager found on the third floor making beds and Jack Lacantro presiding over an empty Young and Jackson's.
- [The canning of the can](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-06-01-batmans-melbourne-the-canning-of-the-can/) — A rash of can-throwing incidents at VFL matches, including a full can hitting a Richmond player and a brawl involving players, spectators and officials at Essendon, has the Premier, the Minister for Sport and the Chief Commissioner of Police all calling for a ban on beer cans at football and cricket grounds, but Keith Dunstan predicts the entirely Australian phenomenon of canspiracy, cantraband and canfusion.
- [Fighting for the fun of it](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-06-08-batmans-melbourne-fighting-for-the-fun-of-it/) — Melbourne's new War Games House, claimed to be the only building in the world entirely devoted to war games, features piped martial music, 300 members re-fighting battles from Waterloo to the hypothetical Sino-Soviet war, while its associated Viking Society stages full-scale axe-and-shield battles for $4 a minute a head, going through three shields in a single six-minute duel.
- [There'll always be an England...](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-06-15-batmans-melbourne-there-ll-always-be-an-england/) — Russell Braddon's television declaration that Anglo-Australian friendship is as dead as the Anzacs prompts Keith Dunstan to survey the many ways England remains inescapable in Melbourne, from the new State governor's Gilbert-and-Sullivan ceremony to Rolls-Royces in Toorak, Oxon-accredited teachers and an English-born headmaster at Geelong Grammar, concluding that the love-hate relationship has simply continued in the same style for 150 years.
- [Hooked on the blurbs](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-06-29-batmans-melbourne-hooked-on-the-blurbs/) — A projectionists' strike closes Melbourne's cinemas for weeks, sending Keith Dunstan, a self-confessed 'advertiolic', back through Thursday-night newspaper archives from February to May, tracing the evolution of movie advertising from Theda Bara in 1916 through covered-wagon spectaculars of the 1920s to the R-rated massage parlour and nymphomaniac blurbs of 1974, concluding the ads are more exciting than the films themselves.
- [Urban butchery in Brisbane](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-07-06-the-cities-urban-butchery-in-brisbane/) — The Queensland Department of Works strips the iron-lace verandahs from Brisbane's 1884 Belle Vue Hotel, claiming a 'public safety hazard', while the National Trust accuses the minister of deliberately humiliating the building after refusing to allow an inspection, in the latest act of the city's long record of aggressive architectural destruction.
- [Excitement in the air](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-07-13-batman-goes-walkabout-excitement-in-the-air/) — Bush Pilots Airways of Cairns, started in 1951 with a single Tiger Moth and now operating five DC3s on a weekly New Guinea tour for $275 all-inclusive, takes Keith Dunstan and retired passengers through Lae, Rabaul, Madang and Port Moresby, where snorkelling off a New Yorker-cartoon island leads one woman to reflect on the Allied campaign in the Pacific.
- [Riding the ritzy rattler](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-07-20-batmans-melbourne-riding-the-ritzy-rattler/) — Taking the overnight train to Sydney, where nobody frisks you, the dining car serves mushroom soup and entrecote while Melbourne's lights recede, and the conductor folds your bed and asks about your morning tea, Keith Dunstan commends a journey that ends at Central Station at 9 am, fresh to begin the day, though showering in a twinette roomette calls for particular skills.
- [The language of screwballs](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-07-27-batmans-melbourne-the-language-of-screwballs/) — Frank Sinatra's use of 'hooker' to describe female journalists at Festival Hall sends Melbourne newsrooms to their dictionaries, while a letter from 'Irate Purist, Dandenong' prompts Keith Dunstan to consult Roget's Thesaurus for clean alternatives to queer, fairy, screw, pervert, bang, pot, intercourse, grass, fuzz, boob and other words that cause constant sniggering, before turning to the parlous shortage of genuine swear words.
- [Drink your way round the world](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-08-03-batmans-melbourne-drink-your-way-round-the-world/) — The rise of special-interest tours, butterfly tours, wine and gourmet tours through Bordeaux, Burgundy and Napa Valley, an archaeology tour led by a Melbourne University reader, and a Dalgety world wool study tour taking buyers to Moscow and Belgrade, prompts Keith Dunstan to imagine a 1974 version offering to get travellers ambushed in Israel, bombed in Beirut, tarred and feathered in Ulster and driven through the jungles of Laos.
- [The noble game on the big screen](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-08-10-batmans-melbourne-the-noble-game-on-the-big-screen/) — With VFL attendance at its lowest since the war years and the ABC television series 'And the Big Men Fly' attracting protests over piled-on violence, Stoney Creek Films launches a $250,000 adaptation of Barry Oakley's 'A Salute to the Great McCarthy', with Barry Humphries as club president Colonel Ball Miller, including a stunt requiring John Jarrat to leap from a seven-storey building in South Yarra.
- [Averting a beer shortage tragedy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-08-17-batmans-melbourne-averting-a-beer-shortage-tragedy/) — A transport strike leaves Melbourne without beer, prompting Keith Dunstan to relate his experiences with home brewing, keeping the fermenter warm through Melbourne's coldest winter in a decade by dismantling his bedside lamp, trying the hot water service, then pressing an electric blanket into service outdoors, while Sydney beer crosses the border by night in closed trucks at twice the normal barrel price.
- [Trams across the border](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-08-24-batmans-melbourne-trams-across-the-border/) — Sydney's consideration of re-introducing trams prompts Keith Dunstan to celebrate Melbourne's tram revival, a new $120,000 orange tram on Bourke Street, rising ridership for the first time in 20 years, and trams promoted as a tourist attraction, with Barry Humphries hosting a tram party to Wattle Park for a yellow-themed lunch, reciting his poem 'The Wattle Park Blues.'
- [Victoria's $1.75m history spend-up](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-08-31-batmans-melbourne-victoria-s-1-75m-history-spend-up/) — The Victorian Government's $500,000 combined with a Federal Tourism grant of $1.25 million funds a wave of folk museums and historical recreations, Echuca's riverboat waterfront, Bendigo's Chinese village Dai Gum San, Castlemaine's goldfields museum, Warrnambool's maritime village, as midnight raids by shire councillors scour the countryside for log cabins and steam tractors, though a worrying uniformity of antique cash registers and pioneer pharmacies is creeping in.
- [Garden gnomes in striped suits?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-09-07-batmans-melbourne-garden-gnomes-in-striped-suits/) — The Sun Homes Show at Exhibition Building reveals a rampant nostalgia wave: Carroll and Richardson's authentically reproduced advertising mirrors from Carlton Brewery and Hutton's Hams at $95 each, Eltham Stoves' cast-iron reproductions of Crown fire stoves and pot-belly stoves, gas garden lamps in copper with silver eagles, until an Aboriginal leader protests at stone Aboriginal garden figures and demands European gnomes in striped suits instead.
- [Moral lectures by footy writers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-09-14-batmans-melbourne-moral-lectures-by-footy-writers/) — North Melbourne's Keith Greig wins his second consecutive Brownlow Medal, receiving 58 times more coverage than Patrick White's Nobel Prize, but Richmond Football Club secretary Alan Schwab calls it a joke and says the system must be changed, triggering pointed responses from the Herald's sports editor and letters to The Age, all of which demonstrate that in 1974 Victorian football is where moral problems are most superbly debated.
- [Driven close to a breakdown](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-09-21-batmans-melbourne-driven-close-to-a-breakdown/) — With three family members simultaneously pursuing driving licences under Victoria's new Learner Driver Permits Act, costing $140 and months of agony for a neighbour's daughter, Keith Dunstan surveys Melbourne's 780 driving schools, the ruthless battle to be first in the phone book producing the A.A.A.A.AAABAAABAAA Driving School, and the psychological impossibility of a parent teaching their own child when a gear grind is a shaft through the heart.
- [It wouldn't have done for Harry!](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-09-28-batmans-melbourne-it-wouldn-t-have-done-for-harry/) — The triumphs of loudmouth self-promoters, Evel Knievel conning $6 million for a canyon motorcycle stunt, Muhammad Ali's $100 million world television deal, Jimmy Connors declaring himself number one at 22, lead Keith Dunstan to mourn the useful skills never taught at his boarding school, where achievement without visible effort was admired and Harry Wharton of the Magnet was the ideal, and to note that only Alan Bond has the appropriate lip for today's world.
- [They stayed away in droves](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-10-05-batmans-melbourne-they-stayed-away-in-droves/) — The Anti-Football League sells 75,000 non-tickets at 20 cents each, including seats in the all-male members' stand and Bay Nine, raises record profits, and stages a coffin burial at sea off Williamstown with Cyril Pearl and Royce Hart's football, though the football escapes the coffin in a gale and skids toward Port Phillip Heads; the Wilkie Medal for taking football off the air goes to Channel Nine's Leon Hill.
- [The case of the deductible dog](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-10-12-batmans-melbourne-the-case-of-the-deductible-dog/) — Adelaide's Dr Colin Ashton wins a $72 tax deduction for his Dalmatian Brod as a burglar alarm, prompting Keith Dunstan to audit the security credentials of the dogs in his street, a great Dane with an inferiority complex, a St Bernard who licks you to death, a bulldog desperate for affection, an afghan who steals cat dishes and laughs about it, and a poodle named Claude who knocks off at 10pm, concluding that medical expenses for dogs should also be tax-deductible.
- [Enough to make a man flake out](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-10-19-batmans-melbourne-enough-to-make-a-man-flake-out/) — Melbourne's three million shark-eating humans, some consuming flake 14 or 15 times a week, face a second crisis after the Victorian Health Minister seizes $20,000 worth of school shark for exceeding the 0.5 parts per million mercury limit, two years after a similar ban; a letter to the Herald demands to know how many Melburnians have actually died from flake and suggests labelling it 'Eating Bolte is a health hazard.'
- [Divvying up the goodies](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-10-26-batmans-melbourne-divvying-up-the-goodies/) — A 24-page brochure of 'Spirit Messages from Mr Lang Hancock' and Queensland Premier Bjelke-Petersen's declaration of his own Queen and anthem send Keith Dunstan to contemplate Australian defederation, with Bjelke-Petersen keeping Amberley air base and F111s, NSW inheriting the Royal Australian Navy, Victoria getting Puckapunyal and 20 tanks, and Western Australia defended by Alan Bond's America's Cup fleet, and the creation of a Disneyland in Canberra called Politicland.
- [It isn't cricket but it's an art](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-11-09-sport-it-isn-t-cricket-but-it-s-an-art/) — As the MCC tour opens on a miserably wet day, confirming another season of meteorological writing, Keith Dunstan surveys the craft of wet-weather cricket reportage from Neville Cardus's Fifth Test meditations to the Port Lincoln press box watching the Ali-Foreman fight on television, while English writers note that Australia perversely stages Tests only in high-rainfall coastal cities when the dry centre might solve everything.
- [Topweight of turf books](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-11-16-batmans-melbourne-topweight-of-turf-books/) — The Australasian Book of Thoroughbred Racing, 453 pages, $19.95, with chapters by Bart Cummings, Roy Higgins, Scobie Breasley, T. J. Smith and Lady Clarke, includes the story of how Lady Clarke's family bet on Counsel for the Caulfield Cup through bookie Phil Moon, Sir Frank Packer chasing a committeeman around the birdcage with an umbrella, and jockey Roy Higgins naming Light Fingers as the best horse he ever rode.
- [Breaking the grass barrier](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-11-23-batmans-melbourne-breaking-the-grass-barrier/) — After 25 years of pushing Churchill, a solid steel-wheeled 1949 hand mower resembling a 28-ton tank, through record Melbourne spring grass, Keith Dunstan surrenders and buys a bright orange two-stroke motor mower, entering a world of prestige trade-ins, auto-drive luxury, ride-on models with twin headlights, and motor-mower mileage tests, before forming the Veteran Lawn Mower Club of Australia to rescue Churchill before he reaches $1000 at Christie's.
- [When Disney comes to town](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-11-30-batmans-melbourne-when-disney-comes-to-town/) — Australia's first Walt Disney production, Ride a Wild Pony, budget $1 million, filming around Chiltern near Wodonga, sends 30 vehicles of crew including cinematographer Jack Cardiff to cover the bitumen roads with earth, repaint all the shops in gold and black, install antique Plume and Atlantic petrol pumps and create a Crystal Palace Theatre with Pola Negri posters, transforming a nearly-demolished country town into a 1928 period piece that Disney plans to leave intact as a tourist attraction.
- [How to Enjoy Hot Christmases](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/readers-digest/1974/how-to-enjoy-hot-christmases/) — A defence of the Australian habit of serving roast turkey and plum pudding in midsummer heat, tracing Keith Dunstan's own Melbourne Christmases from the 1880s boom-era house of his childhood to a flying doctor's Christmas at Mt Isa, an Antarctic station's six-bottle dinner, and a Barrier Reef yacht.
- [The sweet smell of abstinence](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-12-07-batmans-melbourne-the-sweet-smell-of-abstinence/) — The Quit Club's first public meeting draws 200 reformed nicotine addicts to Melbourne's State Film Centre, where members with purple-tongue novice badges share cold turkey strategies, group telephone networks and minute-by-minute watch-gazing techniques, while Dr Nigel Gray of the Anti Cancer Council screens banned anti-smoking commercials including Warren Mitchell's Alf Garnett coughing fit, Freddie Parslow smoking more ruggedly than John Wayne before a lung X-ray, and the now-banned 'Till Death Us Do Part' poster.
- [A testing time for dog people](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1974/1974-12-14-batman-at-the-gabba-a-testing-time-for-dog-people/) — The Queensland Greyhound Owners and Trainers' Association threatens a black ban after spectators at the First Test dropped beer-can tops and broken glass on their dog track, while Keith Dunstan surveys the 'Gabba's transformation from a mound of red dirt under Moreton Bay figs to a ground with grandstands, petunia beds, barbecue facilities and excellent Press box, proposing Test matches and dog races could be run simultaneously, and noting the new innovation of foam car fridges being broken over heads on a Saturday afternoon.
- [Among sovereign citizens](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-01-04-batmans-melbourne-among-sovereign-citizens/) — Keith Dunstan travels to the Hutt River Province, where former wheat farmer Leonard Casley has declared a principality on his 18,500-acre property, issuing passports, stamps and a national anthem, and profiting handsomely from the tourist trade.
- [The Calivil Stakes](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-01-11-batmans-melbourne-the-calivil-stakes/) — At the Calivil foot race near Bendigo, Keith Dunstan witnesses a man named Malcolm Freemantle defeat a camel over 400 metres, along with contests involving donkeys, a steer, and a Shetland pony, in what is described as Australia's most unusual sporting event.
- [The Kooyong veterans](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-01-18-batmans-melbourne-the-kooyong-veterans/) — At Kooyong's grand masters tennis tournament, Keith Dunstan watches veterans including Frank Sedgman, Rex Hartwig, Mervyn Rose and John Davidson demonstrate that great tennis technique does not desert a champion, while the crowd delights in champions who once thrilled them in their prime.
- [Sport gets the union habit](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-01-25-batmans-melbourne-sport-gets-the-union-habit/) — Trade unionism is spreading to sport, with the VFL Players' Association growing in strength and cricketers demanding compensation for advertising on their uniforms, raising the prospect of players striking for better conditions and pay.
- [The art of being nostalgic](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-02-01-batmans-melbourne-the-art-of-being-nostalgic/) — Keith Dunstan finds nostalgia in a Thomas Records shop selling old 78rpm discs, in Tarzan comic books illustrated by Burne Hogarth, and in a 1923 Foy and Gibson catalogue, and argues that in an anxious present the past has never seemed more attractive.
- [When the earth moved](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-02-08-batmans-melbourne-when-the-earth-moved/) — Keith Dunstan attends the Sunbury Pop Festival and is confronted by Deep Purple, reportedly the loudest band in the world, performing at 24,000 watts to a crowd of young people in the mud, with entertainer Denise Drysdale providing a vivid contrast in styles.
- [The secret of long life](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-02-22-batmans-melbourne-the-secret-of-long-life/) — Keith Dunstan debunks health food myths with help from Percy Cerutty and Murray Rose, while celebrating the longevity of old sailor Charlie Rouse, who survived to 94 on the ship Polly Woodside, and concludes that moderate alcohol consumption may be the true key to a long life.
- [Donald Friend in Bali](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-03-01-batmans-melbourne-donald-friend-in-bali/) — Keith Dunstan visits Australian artist Donald Friend at his house in Bali, where Friend lives surrounded by servants, works of art and exotica, including a rotary clothes hoist he has had made from bamboo, and where he holds court far from the Australian art world.
- [Fifty years of the Tiger Moth](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-03-08-batmans-melbourne-fifty-years-of-the-tiger-moth/) — At Casey Airfield near Melbourne, an air pageant marks the Tiger Moth's fiftieth anniversary, with veteran aviator Nancy Bird taking to the air alongside Esther Mather and spectacular aerobatics from a Pitts Special, celebrating the biplane that trained a generation of RAAF pilots.
- [The Bendigo Easter Fair](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-03-15-batmans-melbourne-the-bendigo-easter-fair/) — Keith Dunstan visits Bendigo's Easter Fair, dominated by the magnificent Chinese dragon Sun Loong with its 60,000 mirrors, led by Dennis O'Hoy, while the new Dai Gum San wax museum created by Vivian Sun celebrates the Chinese contribution to Bendigo's goldfields history.
- [Moomba and its problems](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-03-22-batmans-melbourne-moomba-and-its-problems/) — Moomba 1975 sees entertainer Rolf Harris crowned king, but the festival faces familiar controversies, with the rubbish collectors' strike threatening the event and critics questioning whether a festival whose name means 'let's get together and have fun' has lived up to that promise, as previous kings including Robert Helpmann have discovered.
- [The 250th birthday of Remy Martin](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-03-29-batmans-melbourne-the-250th-birthday-of-remy-martin/) — To mark the 250th anniversary of Remy Martin cognac, Melbourne hosts André Heriard Dubreuil, heir to the cognac house, who presides over a tasting of an extraordinarily rare 150-year-old cognac, prompting Keith Dunstan to reflect on the extraordinary longevity possible in great spirits.
- [The new interest in gardens](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-04-05-batmans-melbourne-the-new-interest-in-gardens/) — Melbourne's Garden Week reveals a boom in the garden business, with compost bins, terrariums, ferns and palms all selling briskly, while garden gnomes and Mallee roots enjoy an unexpected revival, suggesting that in uncertain times Australians are finding comfort in cultivating their own patch.
- [The Mildura sculpture show](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-04-12-batmans-melbourne-the-mildura-sculpture-show/) — At Mildura's sixth Sculpture Exhibition, arts director Tom McCullough has assembled an eclectic collection including Don Walters' X-Mass sculpture and Kevin Mortensen's delicatessen installation, in a show that provokes the community's predictable range of reactions from bewilderment to enthusiasm.
- [MCG versus VFL Park](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-04-19-batmans-melbourne-mcg-versus-vfl-park/) — The debate over whether the VFL grand final should leave the Melbourne Cricket Ground for Waverley Park intensifies after a preliminary final is played at VFL Park, with Keith Dunstan examining the MCG's history as a 120,000-capacity ground and arguing that moving the grand final would be an act of civic self-destruction.
- [Quintaphonic and other sounds](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-04-26-batmans-melbourne-quintaphonic-and-other-sounds/) — The film Tommy is being shown in quintaphonic sound at the Esquire cinema, using a system invented by Melbourne's John Mosely, while Keith Dunstan reflects on the generation gap in music, from Deep Purple at Sunbury to Tommy to the Rolling Stones, and wonders what has become of melody.
- [The Godfather comes to Melbourne](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-05-03-batmans-melbourne-the-godfather-comes-to-melbourne/) — The production team for Godfather II, including producer Gray Frederickson, casting director Fred Roos and production designer Dean Tavoularis, arrives in Melbourne to scout locations and discuss the film's spectacular killing sequences, bringing Hollywood's most prestigious franchise to Australia.
- [The opal town](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-05-03-lifestyle-the-opal-town/) — Keith Dunstan visits Andamooka, the South Australian opal mining town where Rudi Duke has built a stubby hotel into an unlikely desert institution, prospector Frank Douglas hunts opals in the barren landscape, and promoters dream of holding a car race across the dry bed of Lake Torrens.
- [The merging of the schools](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-05-10-batmans-melbourne-the-merging-of-the-schools/) — The merger of Clyde School at Woodend with Geelong Grammar, and the Hermitage's merger with another school, mark an economically driven movement toward co-education in Australian private schools, with Keith Dunstan examining what is gained and lost when single-sex boarding schools become co-educational.
- [The serials we loved](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-05-17-batmans-melbourne-the-serials-we-loved/) — Keith Dunstan recalls the golden age of radio serials, Tarzan on 3UZ, the Lone Ranger, the Green Hornet, and the rituals of childhood listening, arguing that the old radio serial produced a quality of imagination that television can never replicate.
- [The Monopoly game](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-06-14-batmans-melbourne-the-monopoly-game/) — Keith Dunstan revisits the history of Monopoly, tracing the board game's invention by Charles Darrow during the Depression, while noting the unexpected cultural battleground between British Airways and Lufthansa whose advertising war echoes Monopoly's property-acquiring logic, and the export of the Australian television series Number 96 to Belgrade.
- [The dentist turned crusader](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-06-21-batmans-melbourne-the-dentist-turned-crusader/) — Alan Russell, a Maroochydore dentist who gave up his practice to become a full-time moral crusader, runs a printing press, campaigns against pornography and regularly telegrams politicians, representing a tradition of passionate individual protest that Keith Dunstan finds both admirable and exasperating.
- [Women on the warpath](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-07-05-batmans-melbourne-women-on-the-warpath/) — In International Women's Year, Keith Dunstan examines the aggressive new female roles in films such as Shampoo, Alvin Purple and Petersen, finding that the liberated woman in Australian cinema is a more predatory figure than her 1950s predecessor, and wondering what Warren Beatty makes of it all.
- [The satirist at work](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-07-12-batmans-melbourne-the-satirist-at-work/) — Amid the constitutional crisis of 1975, Keith Dunstan imagines a satirical Australian state in which journalists and politicians are jailed and caves are named after Ozakitsch Company products, drawing on the confrontation between Gough Whitlam and Malcolm Fraser to explore the limits of political satire.
- [The brawl at Windy Hill](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-07-19-batmans-melbourne-the-brawl-at-windy-hill/) — A brawl between Essendon and Carlton players at Windy Hill results in nine reported players, prompting Keith Dunstan to call on Monash University historian Professor Ian Turner's theory of football as social catharsis, while also noting the simultaneous opening of the film Jaws in Melbourne.
- [The first Ashes Test](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-07-26-batmans-melbourne-the-first-ashes-test/) — The opening Ashes Test in England produces the customary hyperbole from British newspapers, with Dennis Lillee and Jeff Thomson making Mike Denness's batting order look fragile, while Tony Greig's belligerent approach and Keith Dunstan's survey of newspaper coverage reveals the gap between English hope and Australian confidence.
- [The wine test match](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-08-02-batmans-melbourne-the-wine-test-match/) — The Options Club of New South Wales, captained by Len Evans, travels to Melbourne to face Victoria in a wine test match at the Two Faces restaurant, with Victoria winning 129 runs to 125 and receiving the St Vincent's trophy in a contest that takes cricket's ceremonial language and applies it, with great seriousness, to tasting blind.
- [The fate of Flinders Street Station](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-08-09-batmans-melbourne-the-fate-of-flinders-street-station/) — The long history of proposals to redevelop Flinders Street Station, stretching back to 1883, reaches a new chapter with the National Trust fighting to preserve the building, while Norm Gallagher of the BLF demands that any redevelopment include a tavern bar, in a debate that touches on Melbourne's architectural identity.
- [Xavier Herbert](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-08-09-personalities-xavier-herbert/) — Keith Dunstan profiles Xavier Herbert, author of Capricornia, who has spent years in seclusion near Cairns completing Poor Fellow My Country, an 850,000-word novel weighing four and a half pounds, which Herbert's wife Sadie has typed entirely by hand, and which the author believes is his life's greatest work.
- [The science fiction convention](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-08-30-batmans-melbourne-the-science-fiction-convention/) — Melbourne hosts the 33rd World Science Fiction Convention, bringing to the city science fiction editor and archivist Forrest J. Ackerman, Mr Sci-fi himself, alongside writer Ursula Le Guin and fan Wilson 'Bob' Tucker, with an Enterprise starship game proving the convention's most popular attraction.
- [Football becomes a business](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-09-06-batmans-melbourne-football-becomes-a-business/) — The VFL launches a properties division to coordinate club merchandising, gas stoves, money boxes and other branded goods, following a plan developed by advertising agency J. Walter Thompson, with North Melbourne's sponsorship deal with Courage Brewery serving as the new commercial model for Australian Rules Football.
- [The massage parlour debate](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-09-13-batmans-melbourne-the-massage-parlour-debate/) — Melbourne now has 116 massage parlours, and the debate over their regulation has produced a government report titled Victoria Gets the Massage, with planning minister Rupert Hamer banning new parlours from residential areas while the existing ones continue to operate in a legal grey area across the city.
- [Taxing the vices](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-09-20-batmans-melbourne-taxing-the-vices/) — The Victorian budget debate produces fanciful proposals to tax pornography and massage parlours as a revenue source, with Keith Dunstan examining the R-certificate film business, the film Histoire d'O and the difficulty of drawing lines between acceptable and unacceptable material in a permissive age.
- [The dog show](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-09-27-batmans-melbourne-the-dog-show/) — At the Melbourne Royal Dog Show, Afghan hounds dominate the entries with 300 dogs competing, Irish setters are staging a resurgence over German shepherds, and judge Bill Crowley presides over what Keith Dunstan describes as the most socially revealing event in Melbourne's dog calendar.
- [Kryal Castle](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-10-04-batmans-melbourne-kryal-castle/) — Businessman Keith Ryall has built Kryal Castle near Ballarat, a recreation of a medieval fortress complete with a torture chamber and chastity belts, while the story of Lola Montez and editor Harry Seekamp's battle over her dancing gives the region a genuine historical echo, as does the Old Sydney Town reconstruction near Gosford.
- [Men who cry](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-10-11-batmans-melbourne-men-who-cry/) — The emergence of emotional displays in public, Gary Dempsey crying on the football field, North Melbourne supporters weeping at their premiership victory, cricketers hugging each other, prompts Keith Dunstan to examine changing expectations of male emotional expression, contrasting this with Leonid Brezhnev kissing Henry Kissinger.
- [The denim revolution](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-10-18-batmans-melbourne-the-denim-revolution/) — Faded denim fashion has conquered Toorak as much as the working class, with a midnight movie session at a Toorak cinema full of denim-clad patrons, while Keith Dunstan proposes an Anti-Jeans Association and notes that the opening of Rhodes Scholarships to women is a greater revolution than any change in fashion.
- [The bicycle boom](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-10-25-batmans-melbourne-the-bicycle-boom/) — Melbourne is experiencing an unprecedented bicycle boom, with Malvern Star releasing a limited-edition Sovereign Star at $560 and European racers like Peugeot and Raleigh selling out, though the lack of bicycle paths in Melbourne remains a serious impediment to the expansion of cycling as a practical means of transport.
- [The royal visit](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-11-08-batmans-melbourne-the-royal-visit/) — Princess Margaret's visit to Victoria provides Keith Dunstan with the occasion to recall his experience covering Royal Tours, including the elaborate movement orders and code names, the racing at Moonee Valley, and the impractical suggestion that the royal party be taken to the Newmarket abattoir as an educational experience.
- [The crisis in literature](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-11-15-batmans-melbourne-the-crisis-in-literature/) — The 1975 constitutional crisis inspires a survey of the literary allusions being deployed by both Whitlam and Fraser supporters, with an Ovid quotation surfacing alongside comparisons to Caligula, a Richard III Society mobilising, and Percy Shelley being misquoted in a political advertisement.
- [Lashings of entertainment](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-11-29-batmans-melbourne-lashings-of-entertainment/) — At Old Sydney Town near Gosford, Keith Dunstan watches convict re-enactments including a public flogging of Jane Jones twice daily, performed in a half-built St Phillip's Church by actors including Eric Thiison in the role of a convict, while the 80-foot brig Perseverance serves as the centrepiece of the colonial settlement.
- [The sad saga of Toby Mick](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-12-06-batmans-melbourne-the-sad-saga-of-toby-mick/) — The opening of Jaws in Melbourne prompts Keith Dunstan to announce his own rival project: a novel called Teeth and a film by Tim Burstall about the Australian school shark, following Toby Mick, an innocent 37-inch shark navigating mercury contamination, Mentone fish and chip shops and the spear fishermen hired to catch him.
- [Have you been asked lately?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-12-13-batmans-melbourne-have-you-been-asked-lately/) — As the 1975 federal election approaches, Keith Dunstan notices that unlike previous elections, when everyone from academics to kangaroo lovers signed full-page newspaper advertisements, nobody has asked him to sign anything this time, and he proposes organising 999 alderpersons and artists to publish their voting intentions in the Australian.
- [Going through bitter times](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-12-20-batmans-melbourne-going-through-bitter-times/) — A beer strike has left 75 percent of Victoria's hotels dry, with 120,000 casual workers stood down and extraordinary scenes of drinkers chasing Courage Brewery trucks through the suburbs, as Keith Dunstan surveys the drinking statistics showing beer accounts for 17.5 percent of all liquid consumed and the state endures a drought worse than Christmas 1962.
- [The best time](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1975/1975-12-27-batman/) — Keith Dunstan recalls his best times, the girls' school dance where he danced every dance with Priscilla, only to fail to recognise her at a ball twenty-five years later, alongside a Christmas Day 1950 flight with Prime Minister Robert Menzies from Singapore to Calcutta, where the BOAC steward announced that time had become irrelevant and proposed a Courvoisier before dinner.
- [Two Up in a black tie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-01-10-batmans-melbourne-two-up-in-a-black-tie/) — A visit to the legal Two Up game at Wrest Point Casino in Hobart, where the spinner is in black tie, the ring is padded with royal blue carpet, and Keith Dunstan foul-tossed three times before slinking away from the national game in humiliation.
- [Melbourne cut by the Fraser line](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-01-17-batmans-melbourne-melbourne-cut-by-the-fraser-line/) — The Federal election results have split Melbourne cleanly along the Yarra, with Liberal blue on the wealthy south and east and Labor grey across the working-class north and west, producing a battle map that resembles the fall of Europe to the Germans in 1940.
- [A nose wheelie, a tail wheelie](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-01-24-batmans-melbourne-a-nose-wheelie-a-tail-wheelie/) — American skateboard champion Stacy Peralta visits Melbourne for a demonstration session in a multi-storey car park, performing nose wheelies, tail wheelies and terrifying downhill slaloms that reveal a sport combining the grace of Nureyev with the daring of a dive bomber.
- [Melbourne returns to silent Sundays](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-02-14-batmans-melbourne-melbourne-returns-to-silent-sundays/) — Victoria's new noise control legislation sets decibel limits for lawnmowers, power tools and amplified music, prompting a rooftop test session that reveals the four-stroke Rover mower as the suburban Sunday's prime villain at 91 decibels, while Melbourne simultaneously prepares to welcome the Concorde.
- [Champagne in the BYO belt](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-02-28-good-living-champagne-in-the-byo-belt/) — Len Evans launches a French champagne award over eight morning tastings at Two Faces restaurant, as Melbourne's booming BYO restaurant scene faces a legal challenge from licensed restaurateurs who want the government to either fully licence all restaurants or abolish the bring-your-own permit entirely.
- [Slugging it out with snails](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-03-06-batmans-melbourne-slugging-it-out-with-snails/) — After wine merchant Len Evans boasts of eating Sydney park snails, Keith Dunstan attempts to serve home-grown garden snails to his dinner guests, enduring a three-day purification regime, an escaping bucket overnight, and a first tasting that is leathery before the second snail redeems the whole exercise with a glass of dry suburban riesling.
- [Flights of fancy over Jenny...](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-03-20-batmans-melbourne-flights-of-fancy-over-jenny/) — Toy company Toltoys hires a Boeing 747 to secretly launch their new Jenny doll to 365 toy buyers mid-flight over the east coast, with film screens, saturation TV advertising and a duty-free bag for every buyer, while the Sydney Toy Fair also reveals the booming Six Million Dollar Man range and a quarter-million Sindy dolls already sold in Australia.
- [Surviving our biggest wine show](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-10-23-batman-s-melbourne-surviving-our-biggest-wine-show/) — Expovin 76, Australia's biggest international wine exhibition, draws 70,000 visitors to Melbourne's Exhibition Building, where judges from four countries award Wolf Blass a third consecutive Jimmy Watson Trophy and the city narrowly avoids watching its prized fountain flow with 400 gallons of indifferent red wine.
- [Uneasy rider](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-11-06-batman-on-a-bicycle-uneasy-rider/) — Keith Dunstan recounts cycling 6700 kilometres across America as one of 4000 riders in Bikecentennial 76, navigating timber trucks in Oregon, dry Kentucky counties, the cruising ritual in Missouri small towns, and the Hoosier Pass at 3400 metres, guided by Sir Hubert Opperman's advice to keep the chamois well greased.
- [The kookiest Cup of them all](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-11-13-batman-s-melbourne-the-kookiest-cup-of-them-all/) — Melbourne Cup fashions have drifted from morning dress and earnest elegance into deliberate mockery, with protesters targeting Sir John Kerr in anti-formal gear and recycled denim tails, prompting concern that when a society begins to spurn the tribal rituals handed down over generations, it is a sign of decadence.
- [Just a harmless little bit of blood and guts](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1976/1976-11-20-batman-s-melbourne-just-a-harmless-little-bit-of-blood-and-guts/) — A sentimental moviegoer's fruitless search for a decent picture in Melbourne's current release schedule, which offers nothing but demonic children, splatter films, Nazi brothels and sexually transmitted disease comedies, with the only hope a 100-foot gorilla arriving on Christmas Eve.
- [The inversion of a wine snob](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-01-08-batmans-melbourne-inversion-of-a-wine-snob/) — Keith Dunstan confesses his long career as a fake wine expert, from home-bottling in turpentine bottles and pillaging Toorak rubbish bins for empties, through the painful stages of wine snobbery, to his current humiliating attempt to wean himself back to the cheap stuff.
- [I tell you, myxo didn't get 'em all](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-01-15-batmans-melbourne-myxo-didnt-get-em-all/) — A visit to the World Championship Rabbit Skinning Contest at Moyston, population 63, where former world champion "Killer" Crawford, the graceful Ray Bath, and a fearless women's competitor named Doris Tognan demonstrate that the old art of rabbiting is alive and well in pre-myxomatosis scenes just beyond Ararat.
- [A far cry — or yodel — from Bazza](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-01-22-batmans-melbourne-a-far-cry-or-yodel-from-bazza/) — On the set of Bruce Beresford's "The Getting of Wisdom," Barry Humphries plays a pious Presbyterian headmaster while a young Susannah Fowle takes the lead role of Laura, a world away from Bazza McKenzie, with the original PLC demolished and scenes shot at Illawarra's grand staircase.
- [The long march wasn't much longer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-01-29-batmans-melbourne-the-long-march-wasnt-much-longer/) — A China-watcher reports from St Kilda Road on the queues for Melbourne's Chinese exhibition, which is bigger than Blue Poles, bigger than the Modern Masters, and even bigger than King Kong, with the jade suit of Princess Tou Wan drawing reverent crowds and their irreverent commentary.
- [On the money, but very seldom in it](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-01-29-books-on-the-money-but-very-seldom-in-it/) — A review of Ward McNally's biography of Charles Kingsford-Smith, finding it a warmly admiring portrait but too eager to defend its subject, the aviator who was given stingy treatment by both governments and the public despite his heroic achievements, and whose career was largely a series of frustrations.
- [Dame Edna bares all — in limp and stiff](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-02-05-batmans-melbourne-dame-edna-bares-all/) — Dame Edna Everage arrives by Rolls-Royce with a mounted police escort and the Dandenong Marching Grannies to launch her Coffee Table Book, a guide to gracious living featuring funnel web spider cake, Norm's prostate diagram, and poems denouncing Melbourne's massage parlors.
- [The great Australian stupor test](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-03-26-batmans-melbourne-the-great-australian-stupor-test/) — The Centenary Test brought magnificent cricket and magnificent crowds, but also yobs in towelling hats and thongs with eskies the size of coffins, chanting "Lill-ee, Lill-ee" whether Lillee was bowling or not, and booing brilliant cover drives by the opposition.
- [The final passing of the horse](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-04-02-batmans-melbourne-the-final-passing-of-the-horse/) — Melbourne mourns the end of horse-drawn milk deliveries, the last of the 19th century in a city that once had every trade deliver by horse and cart, while a computer expert promises that within five years nobody will be delivering anything at all.
- [The cricket was a booming success](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-04-09-batmans-melbourne-the-cricket-was-a-booming-success/) — The Melbourne Cricket Club revives its 1890s tradition of playing the Walhalla miners at the mountain-top Walhalla Cricket Ground, where sixes are lost forever in the bush, a cannon fires to celebrate wickets, and the MCC is dismissed for 119 before Walhalla United also collapses for 86.
- [The human Melbourne Cup](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-04-23-batmans-melbourne-the-human-melbourne-cup/) — At Stawell's centenary Gift, the professional athletics' Melbourne Cup, Warren Edmondson, a lean Negro from Los Angeles carrying a can of Fosters, psyches himself up for an hour before exploding off the backmark to win, while 94-year-old former champion Chris King recalls that in his day the shorts had to touch the knees for decency.
- [The wowsers still pack a solid vote](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-04-30-batmans-melbourne-the-wowsers-still-pack-a-solid-vote/) — The Pizza Hut at Box Hill discovers what the district's curious dry history already knows, that Camberwell, named after a pub but gone dry in 1920, still returns its local option polls against liquor by a solid majority, even when a pizza chain spends $4000 canvassing every elector.
- [The strike launched a serene cycle](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-05-07-batmans-melbourne-the-strike-launched-a-serene-cycle/) — The tanker strike turned Melbourne briefly into something like Amsterdam, cars banished, bicycles everywhere, the Fitzroy Gardens visible for the first time in years, 91,000 people walking to the MCG for Anzac Day, and road deaths dropping to eight, while the union chief's unlisted namesake in the phone book fielded bomb threats.
- [Practice makes perfect, but not wealth](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-05-14-batmans-melbourne-practice-makes-perfect-but-not-wealth/) — At the first Australian Gold Panning Championships in Bendigo, where world champion Dorse Prosser arrives with his gold pan strapped to his briefcase and 81-year-old Jesse Starnes presides, David Henderson from Eaglehawk wins in 13.1 seconds, though he confesses 40 years of panning has yielded him only three ounces of gold.
- [The FJ Holden is today's ideal car](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-05-21-batmans-melbourne-the-fj-holden-is-todays-ideal-car/) — Prompted by the petrol crisis and President Carter's demands for smaller cars, Keith Dunstan proposes reviving the FJ Holden, weighing seven cwt less than a modern Kingswood, capable of 34 miles to the gallon, and now acquiring a dashing romantic symbolism via a new Australian film.
- [A fight over faded glory](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-06-18-batmans-melbourne-a-fight-over-faded-glory/) — The Regent Theatre sits in comic stalemate, the Municipal Officers' Association banning its reconstruction, the Builders' Laborers banning its demolition, and costing $800,000 a year while doing nothing, with enough colourful characters to cast a perfect film about its long and tortured story.
- [Trying to sell Buckingham Palace](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-06-25-batmans-melbourne-trying-to-sell-buckingham-palace/) — The ordeal of selling a family home, keeping it like Buckingham Palace in jubilee week while buyers arrive at all hours, inspect the dirty washing and criticise the kitchen, and estate agents dress it up with descriptions like "gracious Edwardian home" for a property with chip bath heater, "superb wooded garden" for morning glory holding up the garage.
- [Ideas on holding down the hold-ups](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-07-09-batmans-melbourne-ideas-on-holding-down-the-hold-ups/) — Melbourne's new Tourism Authority launches amid a city famous for being the armed hold-up capital of the world, over 228 armed hold-ups this year, with the State Savings Bank's PR man cataloguing the daily public suggestions: nerve gas, marbles, trap-doors, fall-in grills, dye capsules, radio transmitters in banknotes, and the ejector seat for tellers.
- [The "Old dark blue" goes pink](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-07-16-batmans-melbourne-the-old-dark-blue-goes-pink/) — Melbourne Grammar announces 25 girls will start at Grimwade House next year, a momentous break for Australia's oldest Anglican public school, which has produced three Prime Ministers, while cold economics drives the co-ed trend across Victoria's private schools, with over 200 girls already at Geelong Grammar and female crews heading for the Head of the River.
- [Stagflation is NOT blowing up deer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-07-23-batmans-melbourne-stagflation-is-not-blowing-up-deer/) — On the eve of another budget, with 38 percent of economists optimistic, 28 percent predicting ruin and 34 percent waffling, Keith Dunstan offers a seminar in economic vocabulary, spiralling inflation, stagflation, buoyant or rocky outlooks, haemorrhaging reserves, and the vital concept of "viable", so readers can hold their own at dinner parties.
- [Projects galore but no end in site](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-08-13-batmans-melbourne-projects-galore-but-no-end-in-site/) — An adman proposes harnessing Melbourne's hot air from parliament, the City Council, the BLF and the Save the Regent Committee to power a turbine, which captures the city's crisis of confidence perfectly, as Keith Dunstan opens a form guide on its projects: Collins Place 3/1, underground 100/1, arts centre 250/1, and Newport power station at 1/1992.
- [My house is not, repeat not, a home](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-08-20-batmans-melbourne-my-house-is-not-repeat-not-a-home/) — Moving out of a family home of 20 years in a single day, a chain reaction of Melbourne removalists all shifting at once, becomes an excavation through pogo sticks, hula hoops, cigarette card collections of Woodfull and Cazaly, the Guest House at Lorne photograph trick of sprinting to appear in the panoramic portrait twice, and the children's heartbreak over discarded school essays.
- [That dreadful regiment of joggers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-08-27-batmans-melbourne-that-dreadful-regiment-of-joggers/) — The jogging and fitness craze has swept Melbourne, Lufthansa runs in-flight exercises, Prahran Market fathers arrive in matching crimson tracksuits, Toorak couples commission made-to-measure His-and-Hers wool sets at $80, and even the young attend 21sts in Adidas gear, while Keith Dunstan offers advice on the correct track-suit aesthetic, from the form-fitting leg to the ski resort badge.
- [Is nothing sacred?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-09-03-batmans-melbourne-is-nothing-sacred/) — The Herald reports that Moonee Valley Racing Club may go heterosexual, allowing men and women to mix in the betting rings and bars, which would cascade through Flemington, Caulfield and Sandown, ending Melbourne's cherished tradition of sexual apartheid in the members' enclosures, a curiosity as distinctive as the city's trams.
- [We're in a parlors state](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-09-10-batmans-melbourne-were-in-a-parlors-state/) — A massage parlour has opened in Keith Dunstan's South Yarra street, prompting reflection on how Melbourne has grown from 12 parlours five years ago to around 200, the Town Planning Appeals Tribunal calls them "thinly disguised brothels", while the Sunday Observer's four pages of advertisements offer everything from Tommy with a 48-inch bust to firelight massage and escorts for the discriminating.
- [Cold comfort](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-09-17-batmans-melbourne-cold-comfort/) — A letter from Trans Time Inc. of Canberra prompts a conversation with Australian agent Dr Thomas Donaldson, a mathematics lecturer at the ANU, about cryonic suspension, $50,000 for the full body, $15,000 for the head only, 28 Americans frozen so far with 14 still in thermos-bottle storage at minus 169 degrees, leading Keith Dunstan to doubt whether waking in the year 3000 would be worth the trouble.
- [Twice was two times too much](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-10-08-batmans-melbourne-twice-was-two-times-too-much/) — Melbourne endures two grand finals in a row, Channel 7's football marathon runs from midnight Friday through nine replayed finals and a champagne breakfast before the actual match draws 106,000 to the MCG, leaving wedding guests in St Raphael's Preston exchanging thumb signals about Collingwood's score during the ceremony, and brides displaced to 9 am starts so grooms can still make the game.
- [The dreaded peril from the south](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-10-22-batmans-melbourne-the-dreaded-peril-from-the-south/) — Premier Bjelke-Petersen's warning against Victoria's industrial disease prompts Keith Dunstan to defend his state's close ties with Queensland, Myer, Coles, Carlton Draught and 80 percent of Brisbane business houses, while Premier Hamer's delicate state of emergency during the spring racing carnival leads to a defence consultation revealing that all the Leopard tanks are at Puckapunyal, the paratroopers are in Western Australia, and the best available are 150 Cessnas at Moorabbin.
- [Introducing the no-go road show](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-11-19-batmans-melbourne-introducing-the-no-go-road-show/) — The F19 freeway, $87 million, five lanes each way, passing three golf courses and Fairlea women's prison, sits unused and unloved as citizen co-ordinator Andrew Herington's 800-name telephone tree triggers town hall bells and car-cadaver barricades across Alexandra Parade, while Premier Hamer finally agrees to halt work pending a new study, leaving Keith Dunstan to suggest converting it to 500 tennis courts, 300 basketball courts, or 12 drive-in theatres.
- [How not to go bonkers at election time](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-12-03-batmans-melbourne-how-not-to-go-bonkers-at-election-time/) — Australia's nine legislatures have produced a federal election every second year since Federation, and with both parties spending $2 million on advertising for the current campaign, Keith Dunstan offers the Bulletin Guide to Mental Purity: avoid TV between 6 and 8.30 pm, listen to FM radio (Wagner's Siegfried is safe), throw away your letterbox junk, read newspapers from the back page, and start conversations about whether the Pope would make a good Presbyterian.
- [The colorful cloying of company reports](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-12-10-batmans-melbourne-the-colorful-cloying-of-company-reports/) — Annual reports in 1977 are 22.8 percent bigger than 1976, with color up 29.7 percent, EMI's features a National Geographic seascape and a gentleman wielding an electron into a cathode ray tube, Carlton and United Breweries shows a million empty pottles, BHP's board poses like a Marylebone cricket team of the 1880s, and Peter Kurts Properties labels their executives "DYNAMIC," "A LARGE YOUNG LION," and "NOT EASILY RUFFLED" in the chairman's own handwriting.
- [Please keep on the grass](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-12-17-batmans-melbourne-please-keep-on-the-grass/) — The muesli-and-fitness revolution has overtaken Keith Dunstan's household, 5BX exercises, isometrics, Japanese cookers, vitamin E for immortality, lunchtime joggers fleeing their coronaries through the Treasury Gardens, but after mixing muesli in the bath and graduating to a plastic rubbish bin, the most remarkable result is a stomach like a five-gallon fermenting tank, and the next trend is grasses, herbs and weeds, with nasturtiums recommended to arouse the sluggish man from his torpidity.
- [Come to Sydney and get bitten](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1977/1977-12-24-batmans-melbourne-come-to-sydney-and-get-bitten/) — Melbourne's new Tourism Authority and Sydney's new Visitors Bureau launch simultaneously, Melbourne sends Lord Mayor Kennedy, Cr Rockman, league footballers and local beauties to Hyde Park to give away 2200 carnations and kick footballs into the crowd while playing "Why Don't You Come And See Melbourne" over loudspeakers, prompting Keith Dunstan to propose Sydney reciprocate with mock funnel-web spiders, Manly sharks in a tank, and Madame Justice Evatt as compere.
- [What did YOU do for private enterprise, daddy?](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-01-17-ansett-battle-what-did-you-do-for-private-enterprise-daddy/) — Bob Ansett's relentless battle to break the airport car-hire monopoly held by his father Sir Reginald Ansett's Avis franchise, told through his series of increasingly elaborate PR stunts.
- [I'm sorry, Jim, I can't bare it](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-01-17-batmans-melbourne-im-sorry-jim-i-cant-bare-it/) — Writing from South Yarra as "Batman," Keith Dunstan explains to Jim Cairns in an open letter why his puritan Melbourne upbringing, school-day segregation, and traumatic experience at Hiroshima airport have left him constitutionally unable to participate in nude protests.
- [How to keep Norm in his place](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-01-24-batmans-melbourne-how-to-keep-norm-in-his-place/) — A visit to a friend's new video games set for a "sports evening" reveals the humiliating truth that the future will demand joysticks, speed-up switches, and total defeat at electronic tennis, squash, and shooting games.
- [My secret dossier](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-07-batmans-melbourne-my-secret-dossier/) — "Batman" confesses his ASIO dossier to prove that history shows Australia's real enemies have always come from the right, not the left, by listing his own impeccably conservative credentials including Melbourne Grammar, the Melbourne Club, and devotion to Henry Bolte candles.
- [Something to be done? Get Lillian](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-07-lifestyle-something-to-be-done-get-lillian/) — A portrait of Lillian Frank, Melbourne's flamboyant queen of hairdressing, whose 15-year reign of spectacular fashion at the Cup, seven front pages at Hair's opening night, and newly acquired role promoting Rocky Mattioli's world title fight proves she is as far from shy as Eva Gabor.
- [Getting in the swim, and out of it](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-14-batmans-melbourne-getting-in-the-swim-and-out-of-it/) — The reality of South Yarra swimming pool ownership, an hour's labour a day vacuuming leaves, wrestling with pH levels, replacing pumps at $200 a time, and suffering exploding underwater lights, proves more exhausting than a hectare of lawn.
- [A strange path to rectitude](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-21-batmans-melbourne-a-strange-path-to-rectitude/) — The 1978 Craft Festival opens with Premier Hamer and Eric Westbrook in YOU CAN MAKE IT T-shirts, 10,000 ceramic bricks to decorate, and a stained glass panel for the front door that the wife quietly had a professional redo, leaving Dunstan to wonder if by December the whole city will be praying for the return of Norm.
- [The language takes a mauling](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-28-batmans-melbourne-the-language-takes-a-mauling/) — The opening of the first block of the Bourke Street Mall, complete with orange trams still running through it, prompts a meditation on the word "mall," the years of furious political warfare between Bourke Street and Collins Street factions, and the dream of one day turning Melbourne's entire Golden Mile into a pedestrian paradise.
- [Press-button pastimes](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-02-28-electronics-press-button-pastimes/) — Unitrex Australia managing director Dan Presser returns from the Consumer Electronics Winter Show at Las Vegas to predict a future of family computers, projection TV, and supermarket shopping via digital telephone, while a New York Times man marvels that every living room will soon look like the control room at Newscenter Four.
- [Recalling a great Australian eccentric](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-03-07-batmans-melbourne-recalling-a-great-australian-eccentric/) — A Melbourne University Gallery exhibition marks Percy Grainger's birthday and directs visitors to the remarkable Grainger Museum at the university, a repository Grainger designed and partly built himself, containing his towelling suits, his mother's clothes, freeform music machines, intimate confessions, and 21 PhDs worth of yet-unexplored material.
- [Fast becoming the land of milk and money](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-03-28-batmans-melbourne-fast-becoming-the-land-of-milk-and-money/) — The Victorian Dairy Industry Authority's Big M campaign, four flavoured milk flavours in handy cartons aimed at teenagers, has captured 13 percent of the soft drink market in four weeks, and now they want to put milk cocktails into hotel smorgasbords, served as a Misky or a Cooper Special.
