- [A burning passion for pies](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-04-11-batmans-melbourne-a-burning-passion-for-pies/) — Two visiting food experts, American diet guru Lelord Kordel who condemns pies, and British food scientist Dr Magnus Pyke who enthusiastically endorses them, give Dunstan the perfect excuse to confess a lifelong addiction to junk food, from penny Nestlé bars through liquorice fishing lines to the greatest Melbourne contribution to mankind, the Little Bourke Street dim sim.
- [The drama of beer-bottled wine](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-04-18-batmans-melbourne-the-drama-of-beer-bottled-wine/) — After attending a Brown Brothers Home Bottling Seminar where the winemakers proved a 1962 red sealed with a crown cap beat the same wine under cork, Dunstan overcomes his cultural inhibitions and finally makes the switch, bottling his cabernet-malbec in beer bottles, then wondering if the BYO restaurants will still treat him with charm.
- [The island that isn't a con](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-04-18-travel-the-island-that-isnt-a-con/) — A visit to Kangaroo Island, where tourists must be protected from predatory wildlife, pelicans do high-marking catches like Australian Rules footballers, penguins invade caravans at night, and 1000 kilometres of fiendish dirt roads lead to the discovery that after dark absolutely nothing happens.
- [Making our Sunday a political football](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-04-25-batmans-melbourne-making-our-sunday-a-political-football/) — The Hamer Government has refused Sunday VFL football despite passionate pleas from the league, while soccer referees are being bashed and changing rooms set on fire, leading Dunstan to defend the sanctity of the Melbourne Sunday as a tourist attraction that feature writers from the world's great newspapers have come specially to chronicle.
- [When a mystery put Melbourne on the map](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-05-02-batmans-melbourne-when-a-mystery-put-melbourne-on-the-map/) — The Sun Books reprint of Fergus Hume's 1886 novel The Mystery of a Hansom Cab, which sold nearly a million copies and did more for Melbourne's fame than Nellie Melba, reveals a vanished gas-lit city of Marvellous Melbourne, the Block, Bourke Street's demi-monde, and a murder mystery that kept Batman reading until 3.30 am.
- [Taking the Doomba out of Moomba](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-05-16-batmans-melbourne-taking-the-doomba-out-of-moomba/) — Melbourne Tourism Authority director Sue Calwell fights to change Melburnians' self-deprecating habit of knocking their own city, a habit so ingrained that Barry Humphries' proposal to turn City Square into an abyss called "Doomba" received more press than any promotional campaign.
- [From now on, Horrie suits himself](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-05-23-batmans-melbourne-from-now-on-horrie-suits-himself/) — Horrie Taafe, the unquestionable men's wear fashion czar of Australia who revolutionised Georges and took buying tours to Harrods in the 1930s, is retiring for the third time, to open his own shop at Mona Vale at nearly 80, with his lifelong hatreds of denim, flared trousers and body-hugging shirts intact.
- [Sending our sins interstate](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-05-30-batmans-melbourne-sending-our-sins-interstate/) — The VFL's plan to shift Sunday football to the Sydney Cricket Ground, thus keeping Melbourne's Sundays pure while exporting the violence and mayhem to NSW, leads Dunstan to propose turning Albury-Wodonga into a hermetically sealed national TV sporting capital, freeing Melbourne's Flemington and Randwick for subdivision.
- [These Oranges are no lemons](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-06-06-batmans-melbourne-these-oranges-are-no-lemons/) — A tram traveller of vintage antiquity defends the new Clockwork Orange trams against their hostile press, finding them smooth, silent and an improvement over the old green rattlers, while proposing that decorated tourist trams serve tea and cakes on runs to St Kilda and Toorak, pointing out the grand homes and finest tax dodges along the way.
- [A read that's richly rewarding](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-06-13-books-a-read-thats-richly-rewarding/) — Sir James Darling's autobiography Richly Rewarding illuminates the complex headmaster of Geelong Grammar, his war against school sport, his support for radical teacher Manning Clark, and his relentless self-examination, while T. H. White's posthumous The Book of Merlyn proves a lesser work, its best material having already appeared in The Sword in the Stone.
- [A bridge of beauty, but a toll forever](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-06-20-batmans-melbourne-a-bridge-of-beauty-but-a-toll-forever/) — Melbourne's West Gate Bridge, longer and wider than the Sydney Harbour Bridge, costing ten times its original estimate of eleven million pounds and carrying a toll that has ballooned from the promised 20–25 cents to a likely dollar, is finally complete, beautiful, and needs only a truckie in a semi-trailer to open it and convince Melburnians it's safe to cross.
- [The sport of king-hits](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-06-27-batmans-melbourne-the-sport-of-king-hits/) — Victoria's thumping 100-point State of Origin victory over Western Australia, achieved after Ron Barassi made his players write 300-word essays on why they wanted to play for Victoria, does nothing to ease the growing tension between States, and the VFL's rivalry with the nascent national football competition remains unresolved.
- [Pedalling the case for cyclists](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-06-27-road-safety-pedalling-the-case-for-cyclists/) — After ten years as a daily bicycle commuter averaging 160 kilometres a week, Dunstan surveys the remarkable progress from open hostility and near-wipeouts to the Geelong Bikeplan, the first systematic study of cycling in an Australian city, which has become a blueprint for the nation, backed by $1.6 million in state funding.
- [Hair today, gone to sorrow](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-07-04-batmans-melbourne-hair-today-gone-to-sorrow/) — The Georges Italy 1978 fashion show, with its wet-string hair, Afros, crimped 'electric chair' styles and $45 treatments, confirms Dunstan's fear that hair has not retreated since his brief optimism two years ago, and is now bigger in the economy than drink, tobacco, or any other vice.
- [Cashing in on nostalgia](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-07-11-batmans-melbourne-cashing-in-on-nostalgia/) — The Victorian Government's $100,000 competition for a "Melbourne Monument" to rival the Eiffel Tower prompts Dunstan's winning entry, rebuilding Old Melbourne complete with Cole's Book Arcade, cable trams, the Port Phillip Hotel's punkahs, and all the great Victorian drapery stores with their real counters and real service, a nostalgia trap that would draw tourists by the million.
- [Drinking our way to solvency](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-07-18-batmans-melbourne-drinking-our-way-to-solvency/) — Bob Hawke's public pledge to give up alcohol triggers a meditation on guilt and national finances, the Federal Government raises $475 million on beer and $62 million on spirits, meaning every glass of scotch contributes to some decent lad's public service salary or even the new RAN submarine, a civic duty that wine-drinkers and smokers share in their own way.
- [A footpath foreman's dream comes true](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-07-25-batmans-melbourne-a-footpath-foremans-dream-comes-true/) — A lifetime of building-watching culminates in a two-hour preview tour of the new ANZ Tower in Collins Place, with its 48th-floor boardroom views to Port Phillip Heads, royal-blue carpets, executive bathrooms in white marble, unisex hairdressing salon, sauna, gymnasium, revolving door that stopped a thousand employees moving in for a month, and an underground swimming pool that the nuns never knew how to drain.
- [New horizons for our unique cuisine](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-08-01-batmans-melbourne-new-horizons-for-our-unique-cuisine/) — Premier Dick Hamer's report from Japan, that Westernisation has replaced rice and raw fish with McDonalds and Kentucky Fried, making Japanese children tubby and creating vast cheese demand, leads Dunstan to propose an Australian Trade Delegation introducing Japan to crumpets, dim sims, the barbecue, Vegemite, Violet Crumbles and Eskimo Pies.
- [Living off the fat of the land](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-09-05-batmans-melbourne-living-off-the-fat-of-the-land/) — A road trip up the Newell Highway to Queensland, delayed by a smashed windscreen at West Wyalong, the broken windscreen capital of the world, reveals that Australia is very nearly the worst place for roadside eating, but that the great evolution of the caravan park, with its four-star facilities and heated bathroom floors, now puts more beds in country parks than in motels.
- [A trendy answer to a burning question](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-09-12-batmans-melbourne-a-trendy-answer-to-a-burning-question/) — After moving to a house with Victorian iron grates and marble mantelpieces, Dunstan discovers that going back to open fires means hunting down extinct chimney sweeps, having custom-made ash grates fabricated in sheet metal factories, paying extortionate amounts for a firescreen, foraging in parks for kindling, and hauling wood home in the boot of the car, all worth it for the right to ask snootily at cocktail parties "What do you burn?"
- [Let's hear it for the Mini](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-09-19-batmans-melbourne-lets-hear-it-for-the-mini/) — The announcement that Leyland will stop assembling the Mini in Australia prompts a valediction for a car that has been in Dunstan's family since 1963, still running in querelous health, a machine that could leave V8s at the lights, seat four humans with Russian gymnast flexibility, do 45 miles to the gallon, but never did acquire heating or working windscreen wipers.
- [The great TV screen in the sky](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-09-26-batmans-melbourne-the-great-tv-screen-in-the-sky/) — Melbourne is about to get two enormous outdoor Video Matrix screens, one at the MCG for instant replays at $1 million, and one for the City Square at $1.3 million, raising alarming possibilities about Big Brother, seditious protestors being drowned out by 60-metre images of Dick Hamer, and the death of the great Melbourne custom of meeting your girlfriend "under the clocks" at Flinders Street.
- [For sale: Australia's most magnificent folly](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-10-03-batmans-melbourne-for-sale-australias-most-magnificent-folly/) — Idylwilde, the Balwyn mansion built by chain-store magnate Oliver Gilpin in the 1930s, 230,000 pounds of Japanese gardens, canals, seven stone bridges, 35 aviaries with running water, a deer sanctuary, a hidden indoor swimming pool, and a bathroom the nuns never entered, goes to auction after the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart can no longer afford the $15,000 annual rates.
- [Do it yourself? You have to](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-10-10-batmans-melbourne-do-it-yourself-you-have-to/) — Dunstan announces Batman's Law of Motion, the greater the unemployment, the greater the difficulty in getting anyone to work, illustrated by a leaking roof, a never-built fence, carpenters who demand $740 in cash off the hip, a friend's planning nightmare trying to build a "storeroom" that isn't above ground, and a prediction that by 1990 Australians will be doing all their own carpentry, plumbing and electrics.
- [Knockers held in high regard](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-10-17-batmans-melbourne-knockers-held-in-high-regard/) — Lord Mayor Rockman's campaign against Melbourne knockers, with his proposed "I love Melbourne" bumper stickers and appeals for positive slogans, misunderstands the fundamental psychology of Melburnians, who are kygmies by nature and would draw far more tourists with an international knocking competition than with any amount of civic boosterism.
- [Lunch hour in a tippler's Valhalla](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-10-31-batmans-melbourne-lunch-hour-in-a-tipplers-valhalla/) — Melbourne's Expovin wine exhibition drew 100,000 enthusiasts to its 4½-acre floor of stands serving fine reds, pates and champagne, where Malcolm Fraser sampled only Australian wines, Wolf Blass was first in the queue, the Connoisseurs' Terrace poured 1955 Grange Hermitage, and a battery-powered home-bottling pump replaced the age-old pleasure of sucking on a tube.
- [The fantastic frivolity of the Melbourne Cup](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-10-31-bulletin-cover-story-the-fantastic-frivolity-of-the-melbourne-cup/) — Melbourne goes into a religious trance at Cup time, 300,000 silent Melburnians line Swanston Street for Moomba, but put horses around and anything can happen, with the Catholic writer J. Francis Hogan having made the submission in the 1880s that Australians treat the horse as the only true God, a thesis supported by the fact that Australia has 464 racetemples compared to England's 64.
- [The summer scent of scorched chops](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-11-07-batmans-melbourne-the-summer-scent-of-scorched-chops/) — The annual barbecue season descends on Melbourne with its black pall of smoke, $3000 paved outdoor living spaces with redwood cedar tables, coin-in-the-slot units along the Yarra, the curious male prerogative of actually cooking, and the unfailing rule that the only suitable drink for scorched meat is an incomparably awful rough red out of a plastic bladder.
- [The great Toorak paper war](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-11-14-batmans-melbourne-the-great-toorak-paper-war/) — The discovery that Prahran is Melbourne's top garbage suburb at 6.4 kg per resident per week, against Croydon's virtuous 1.97 kg, leads Dunstan to form the Anti Paper Club, dedicated to leaving shops without wrapping, though progress is slow when shirt boxes require 17 pins and hardware stores regard unwrapped goods as evidence of shoplifting.
- [The artful metamorphosis of a bush town](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-11-21-batmans-melbourne-the-artful-metamorphosis-of-a-bush-town/) — Swan Hill's copybook transformation from a straight-road country town into a year-round tourist mecca, built on the rescued paddlesteamer Gem, a pioneer museum that spawned a continent of imitators, and the new $1.25 million Campbell Street Shopping Park, is crowned by Peter Beattie's Riverboat restaurant, which serves witchetty grub soup canned at Monbulk and ships 60 percent of its production to restaurants in the United States and Japan.
- [The phoenix that rose from the slums](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-11-28-batmans-melbourne-the-phoenix-that-rose-from-the-slums/) — A Melbourne University seminar on the inner suburbs, tracing five periods from migrant gateway to working-class heartland to light industry to postwar Italian and Greek settlement to the current trendy invasion, confronts Dunstan with his own gentrification of a former working-class South Yarra street, complete with cast-iron twiddledy bits, hanging baskets, and three Porsches within 100 metres.
- [The perils of a bicycle built for two](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-12-05-batmans-melbourne-the-perils-of-a-bicycle-built-for-two/) — A two-year odyssey to import a custom-built touring tandem from California, with its Taylor Brothers frame from Stockton-on-Tees, French cantilever brakes, Japanese disc brakes and Italian seat pillars, ends with a $225 air freight bill, $1063 in customs duty, five months of letters to manufacturers and ministers to claim an exemption, and a final cost of $3000 for a bicycle that does everything promised.
- [It started with a whale of an idea](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-12-12-batmans-melbourne-it-started-with-a-whale-of-an-idea/) — Tyrone Malone, the father of truck dragging in the US, who started his empire by deep-freezing a sperm whale and touring it to 15 million people, brings his $150,000 chrome-and-aerofoil Super Boss Kenworth to Calder Speedway for a confrontation with Australian challenger Waltzing Matilda, powered by a Rolls Royce jet from an old Canberra bomber, before 20,000 spectators in 35-degree heat.
- [More dollars going than coming](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1978/1978-12-19-tourism-more-dollars-going-than-coming/) — The Australian Tourist Commission's 1977 Statistical Review reveals that while 563,000 visitors came to Australia, with New Zealand, the UK and Japan leading, nearly twice as many Australians (971,000) went the other way, spending $580 million abroad against visitors' $343 million, with 51.9 percent of arrivals never getting beyond New South Wales and the Japanese moving through in under a week.
- [Feeling the strain of the party frenzy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-01-09-batmans-melbourne-feeling-the-strain-of-the-party-frenzy/) — Keith Dunstan surveys the exhausting social demands of the Christmas party season, from the strain of remembering names after the divorce revolution to a handy list of conversation-starter topics for the desperate guest.
- [The case for conserving the blowey](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-01-16-batmans-melbourne-the-case-for-conserving-the-blowey/) — Dunstan surveys the curious world of indigenous Australian contests, from fly-swatting championships in Eaglehawk to rabbit-skinning at Moyston, before making a tongue-in-cheek case for protecting the blowfly as a uniquely Australian creature.
- [Not just an ordinary, run-of-the-mill academic](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-01-23-batmans-melbourne-not-just-an-ordinary-run-of-the-mill-academic/) — A tribute to Monash University historian Ian Turner, who died on Erith Island on 27 December 1978, former communist, carriage cleaner, jazz lover, Richmond football fanatic, and one of the most gifted lecturers Australia produced.
- [Let's get back to service with a snarl](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-01-30-batmans-melbourne-let-s-get-back-to-service-with-a-snarl/) — Dunstan rails against the American import of compulsory cheerfulness, from "Have a nice day" butchers to name-tagged bank tellers, and laments the passing of the honest Australian grunt.
- [Melbourne's massage industry](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-02-06-the-professions-melbourne-s-massage-industry/) — Social welfare researcher Bronwen Rumbold lifts the lid on Melbourne's reputation as the massage parlour capital of the world, tracing the city's 300-plus parlours, their links to migration patterns and organised crime, and the Social Welfare Department's cautious attempts at reform.
- [Jerilderie gives Ned a fair go](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-02-27-batmans-melbourne-jerilderie-gives-ned-a-fair-go/) — Dunstan reports on the centenary celebrations at Jerilderie, the small New South Wales town Kelly held at gunpoint in 1879, where 1200 revellers danced until dawn and the people showed no self-doubt at all about honouring the outlaw who robbed their bank.
- [Melbourne gets behind Moomba](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-03-06-festivals-melbourne-gets-behind-moomba/) — On its 25th anniversary, Dunstan traces the turbulent history of Moomba, from its disputed Aboriginal name meaning "let's get together and have fun" to the dramas of sinking gondolas, a cable tram wreck, Rolf Harris and the garbage strike, and Mickey Mouse's pie in the face.
- [A serious case of maladjustment](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-03-13-batmans-melbourne-a-serious-case-of-maladjustment/) — Dunstan offers himself as an image consultant to Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser, prescribing contact lenses, a moustache, gay shirts, a cook book, C. J. Dennis poetry readings at Moomba, and a daily bicycle ride to Parliament House.
- [A festival of light beers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-03-27-batmans-melbourne-a-festival-of-light-beers/) — Courage and Carlton have both launched low-alcohol beers in Melbourne, Dunstan taste-tests both and concludes the random breath-test regime is driving a genuine market revolution, though an anomaly in NSW law keeps them out of Sydney.
- [Art lovers in transports of delight](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-04-03-batmans-melbourne-art-lovers-in-transports-of-delight/) — Melbourne has fallen in love with its trams and commissioned six leading artists, including Mirka Mora, Clifton Pugh and Andrew Southall, to paint them as moving canvases; Dunstan explores the resulting "tramurals" and their unlikely origin stories.
- [The era of musical cohabitants](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-04-10-batmans-melbourne-the-era-of-musical-cohabitants/) — The cohabitation revolution has swept through Dunstan's social circle, from the Baptist mother making quilts for her daughter's new arrangement to Californian "palimony" cases, and he proposes the newspapers add Cohabitations and Dehabitations to their classified columns.
- [A dinkum Oz with a love of the wilderness](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-04-17-batmans-melbourne-a-dinkum-oz-with-a-love-of-the-wilderness/) — Percy Trezise, racing cyclist, airline pilot, artist and Aboriginal rock art expert, visits Melbourne to promote the Second World Wilderness Congress in Cairns in 1980 and shares his vision for Cape York Peninsula as the world's greatest wilderness area.
- [Passionate paintings by an old commo](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-04-24-batmans-melbourne-passionate-paintings-by-an-old-commo/) — Noel Counihan, at 65, holds a retrospective exhibition at Realities Gallery in Toorak, the converted church hall where some of us went to kindergarten, and talks about four decades of social-conscience painting, his communist years, street-meeting arrests, and why showing your work is like being naked in a room.
- [The garish grandeur of the bottom end](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-05-01-batmans-melbourne-the-garish-grandeur-of-the-bottom-end/) — The "Chicago end" of Collins Street, the block of William Pitt's exuberant Land Boom buildings including the Rialto, faces a development battle, and Planning Minister Alan Hunt has declared a three-month freeze while a British expert recommends recycling the entire block.
- [How sinful Sydney got Melbourne's Sunday footy](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-05-08-batmans-melbourne-how-sinful-sydney-got-melbourne-s-sunday-footy/) — The VFL finds a creative way around the Victorian Government's Sunday football ban by staging free "Commodore Cup" reserves matches telecast on Channel Seven, while the VFA retaliates and the VFL books the Sydney Cricket Ground for two proper Sunday premiership matches.
- [Pro Hart: a painter as busy as a bull ant](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-05-15-profile-pro-hart-a-painter-as-busy-as-a-bull-ant/) — Dunstan profiles Pro Hart, the Broken Hill mining artist whom critics spurn and the public adores, tracing his childhood correspondence schooling, 15 years underground, the discovery by Kym Bonython, and his current plans for a 15-metre steel bull ant and a salt-pan canvas dropped from a balloon.
- [A lifetime of penance](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-05-22-batmans-melbourne-a-lifetime-of-penance/) — A self-confessed penaholic traces his obsession from the torment of left-handed steel-nib schoolwriting, through confiscated fountain pens, the ballpoint revolution, cartridge pens, and now the new "floating ball", with a stop at Taft's pen shop in Collins Street.
- [All out for National Strike Day](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1979/1979-06-05-batmans-melbourne-ail-out-for-nations-strike-day/) — With Melbourne deep in its annual strike season, railways, power workers, teachers and bank employees all walking out, Dunstan proposes a National Strike Festival in mid-March and outlines his business plan for the Melbourne Strike Emporium, to be headquartered at the Regent Theatre.
- [Paradise revisited](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-courier-mail/1982/1982-08-07-paradise-revisited/) — Returning to Surfers Paradise after nearly 30 years, Keith Dunstan finds the fibro weekenders of the 1950s replaced by white high-rise towers, 'Inspect Now' signs and unsold apartments, and weighs whether the Gold Coast is better for it.
- [Revolution upstages the border war](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1983/1983-03-29-revolution-upstages-the-border-war/) — The Victorian football season opens with a state-of-war atmosphere between Victoria and South Australia over player transfers, while upheaval at Collingwood, a new president from South Yarra, a new captain recruited from South Australia, and a spectacular Guernsey Night, overshadows the interstate dispute.
- [Don't move the grand final to Swan Lake](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1983/1983-10-04-victoria-don-t-move-the-grand-final-to-swan-lake/) — Keith Dunstan argues passionately against the VFL's plan to shift the grand final from the Melbourne Cricket Ground to VFL Park at Waverley, warning that the MCG is woven into Melbourne's soul and that the league is on the verge of a self-immolating decision.
- [Cricket: or going bats about the ball](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1983/1983-12-06-sport-cricket-or-going-bats-about-the-ball/) — An illustrated excerpt from Keith Dunstan and Jeff Hook's new book A Cricket Dictionary, presenting sardonic definitions of cricket terms from Agricultural shot to Zaaaaaaaaaat.
- [True to trams: Melbourne reaps benefits](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1983/1983-12-20-australiana-true-to-trams-melbourne-reaps-benefits/) — Melbourne's loyalty to its tram network is paying off as the city exports vintage W-class trams to Seattle and San Francisco, Elton John buys one for his garden, and a new book celebrates Australia's tramway heritage.
- [The battle of the MCG](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-02-21-batmans-melbourne-the-battle-of-the-mcg/) — The Melbourne Cricket Club faces a deadly battle as the VFL demands Grand Final rights at the MCG, forcing MCC members from their stand, while the government drives reforms on women's membership and threatens legislation, leaving members wondering what equity they have in their own ground.
- [Getting our government on the ball](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-02-28-batmans-melbourne-getting-our-government-on-the-ball/) — Australia is turning into a sportocracy, VFL champion Kevin Bartlett is crowned King of Moomba, footballers seek parliamentary pre-selection, Robert de Castella wins Australian of the Year, and Bob Hawke rides his sporting connections to a record 73 percent approval rating. Keith Dunstan proposes a fully sporting cabinet led by Alan Bond.
- [Governors are on a good wicket](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-03-06-batmans-melbourne-governors-are-on-a-good-wicket/) — Keith Dunstan surveys Australian governors since World War II and finds the job goes overwhelmingly to generals and lawyers, suggesting it is time for imagination, and nominating ABC cricket commentator Alan McGilvray as the ideal candidate.
- [As torpid as Gomorrah on a rainy Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-03-13-batmans-melbourne-as-torpid-as-gomorrah-on-a-rainy-sunday/) — Germaine Greer attacks Melbourne as dull and boring, but Keith Dunstan mourns that the city's magnificent old torpor is being steadily destroyed by Sunday trading, hotel bars, one-day cricket, Collins Street towers, and a Truth newspaper full of explicit sex advertisements that would have shocked Gomorrah itself.
- [The need for kneecappery](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-03-20-batmans-melbourne-the-need-for-kneecappery/) — This has been a vintage summer for knees, Peter McNamara's reconstructed cruciate ligament, Graham Yallop's medial ligament, Garry Sidebottom's knee, leading Keith Dunstan to propose an Australian Foundation of Kneecappery and chairs of Cartilology at our universities.
- [Pari Tab could save us all](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-03-27-batmans-melbourne-pari-tab-could-save-us-all/) — Frank Hardy laments Australia's guilt-ridden TAB with no lavatories or cafe comforts, while Victoria prepares to introduce Pub TAB and Footy TAB, inspiring Keith Dunstan to propose Parl TAB (bet on ministerial resignations and royal commissions), Crick TAB, and Train TAB to get John Cain's Government out of the red.
- [It's always been 'last in is lousy'](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-04-03-batmans-melbourne-it-s-always-been-last-in-is-lousy/) — Professor Geoffrey Blainey warns that Asian immigration is "well ahead of public opinion," prompting Keith Dunstan to survey Australia's long history of racism, from the Chinese, Irish, Italians and Turks to the treatment of Aborigines, and observe that it has always been the latest arrivals who cop it.
- [Americans sure are normal enough to live in Adelaide](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1984/1984-04-03/) — Returning from California, Keith Dunstan argues the United States is one of the most normal places on earth, and that Australian country motel breakfasts, three-ply toast, instant coffee, make a sorry contrast to American roadside hotcakes.
- [Like filling the MCG with objets d'art](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-04-10-batmans-melbourne-like-filling-the-mcg-with-objets-d-art/) — Melbourne's Arts Centre, fifteen years in the making and finally opening in May 1984, gets Keith Dunstan's grand tour, from the underground theatres floating in primeval swamp mud, to Sidney Nolan's gift of 1350 Paradise Gardens paintings written on a plain sheet of paper, to the 75,000 floating brass baubles in the State Theatre ceiling.
- [The bagnio capital of the world](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-04-17-batmans-melbourne-the-bagnio-capital-of-the-world/) — Victoria's Minister for Planning announces the decriminalisation of prostitution in massage parlours, prompting Keith Dunstan to survey Melbourne's long history with the "social evil", from 597 fallen women in 1885, to the Duke of Edinburgh's visit to Sarah Fraser's bagnio in Stephen Street in 1867, to the 190 parlours now serving 60,000 to 70,000 clients a week.
- [How I learned to love my computer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-04-24-batmans-melbourne-how-i-learned-to-love-my-computer/) — After two months of living with a Tandy TRS80 personal computer, Keith Dunstan reports on his turbulent apprenticeship, the joy of silent 5am keystrokes, the terror of losing whole stories to the electronic void, the global-search miracle, and a 75,000-word spelling dictionary that is making Batman copy pure for the first time in 25 years.
- [I've really had an earful...](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1984/1984-05-06/) — A comic survey of the earring boom, from Elton John's diamond studs and Queen Elizabeth II's pearls to the domestic hazards of pierced ears in a household of daughters.
- [Cinders – it's back to the ball](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-05-08-batmans-melbourne-cinders-it-s-back-to-the-ball/) — Keith Dunstan travels by K-class steam locomotive to celebrate the centenary of T94 at the North Williamstown Railway Museum, 21 steam locomotives, a magnificent 1890 Norman car used by Victorian governors and royalty, and a coming Steam Age Australia luxury excursion service modelled on the Orient Express.
- [Stand by as the get-away becomes a give-away](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1984/1984-05-12/) — A tour through airline brochures reveals the extraordinary lengths carriers are going to in 1984 to win custom, from Dom Perignon in Waterford Crystal to Delft liqueur houses and Sony Walkman headsets.
- [A life of domestic bliss](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-05-15-batmans-melbourne-a-life-of-domestic-bliss/) — Keith Dunstan surveys the security-obsessed miseries of modern Melbourne domestic life, deadlocked out of his own house in dirty jeans, keys locked inside a thief-proof car at the seaside, an RACV man defeated after 45 minutes, and a locksmith who charges $70 to work his way in after dark.
- [Know him? We've just kissed.](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1984/1984-05-20/) — A 1984 photograph of Prince Charles kissing Prince Edward on the cheek prompts a survey of the social kissing boom, from Brezhnev lifting Kissinger bodily off the ground to the art of the cocktail party fake-kiss.
- [Australia's longest-running election](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-05-22-batmans-melbourne-australia-s-longest-running-election/) — The Melbourne Anglican diocese has spent nearly a year trying to elect a new archbishop to replace the departed Archbishop Dann, with two board members themselves candidates, constant leaks splitting the board, and an open letter suggesting Alan Bond, his dedication to causes well known, his media image well managed, as a suitable alternative.
- [Pools: a gum tree's favorite friend](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-05-29-batmans-melbourne-pools-a-gum-tree-s-favorite-friend/) — Domestic Bliss No 2, Keith Dunstan's swimming pool, lifted over the house by a crane when first installed, has proved a fountain of misery and expense: pump repairs, chlorine bills, leaves from the liquidambar and the lemon-scented gum, and a pool turned swamp-green while the owners were overseas. A friend in Moorabbin has shown the way, he gave his fibre-glass pool away on a truck and planted roses instead.
- [Let's move Sunday to Saturday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-06-05-batmans-melbourne-let-s-move-sunday-to-saturday/) — Melbourne's cherished sepulchral Sunday is being eroded by incremental liberalisations, Sunday hotel trading, soccer at the MCG, while hardware merchant Frank Penhalluriack wages a ten-year battle from South Caulfield, paying over $130,000 in fines. Keith Dunstan's new campaign: shift everything to Sunday and have absolutely nothing on Saturday.
- [Hollywood's Mr Nearly Normal](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-06-05-the-arts-james-stewarthollywood-s-mr-nearly-normal/) — With James Stewart arriving in Australia to promote a Hitchcock retrospective, Keith Dunstan recalls his Hollywood encounters, a tourist bus driver shrieking at the sight of Stewart's dog outside his ivy-covered Beverly Hills house, the American Film Institute dinner where Henry Fonda recalled Jimmy's flawless career, and Hitchcock's toast to "the one exception" to his rule that actors should be treated like cattle.
- [The Punks at the Automatic Teller](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1984/1984-06-10/) — A visit to Melbourne's punk hairdressers reveals the engineering behind the Apache-strip, the bobtail, and the scrunch, all of it driven not by political protest but by the desire to look like Boy George.
- [The art of spending pennies](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-06-12-batmans-melbourne-the-art-of-spending-pennies/) — The Rialto, William Pitt's magnificent 1891 Victorian Gothic building at the western end of Collins Street, is being recycled into the grand Menzies at the Rialto hotel, but its refurbishment stalls when the Historic Buildings Council insists on preserving the corrugated iron lavatory cubicles at the end of its galleries, arguing they tell the not-so-glorious story of "Smelbourne" in the 1880s, when night-soil men collected waste and the urinals drained into the Yarra.
- [Ned is now among the real money](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-06-19-batmans-melbourne-ned-is-now-among-the-real-money/) — At Glenrowan, insurance broker Bob Hempel has spent $500,000, vastly more than Ned ever stole, creating a Disneyland-style Kelly show with computerised smoke, articulated robots, real rain down a window, a pub going up in flames on hidden gas jets, and Ned himself at the trap door with drums rolling. Business has been beautiful.
- [How the footy is going to the dogs](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-06-26-batmans-melbourne-how-the-footy-is-going-to-the-dogs/) — Weekly VFL attendances have drifted from 9 percent of Melbourne's population in 1930 to 4.45 percent in 1984, five clubs are technically bankrupt, and North Melbourne ruckman Gary Dempsey warns the game is dying. Premier Cain has offered to help enforce player contracts, the VFL president wants a national competition of 16 teams, and international soccer has arrived, Paolo Rossi's dinner seat at the St Kilda Town Hall cost $5000.
- [Shhh! I haven't got a video cassette recorder](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-07-03-batmans-melbourne-shhh-i-haven-t-got-a-video-cassette-recorder/) — Keith Dunstan confesses to being possibly the only person in his street without a video cassette recorder, his wife forbids it, he could not work one anyway, and movie reviewers who send him preview tapes are incredulous. Meanwhile the local petrol station, chemist and Seven-Eleven deli all hire out videos, Victoria has just legalised X-rated tapes, and a friend with the full setup dims the living room after dinner for his private blue-movie screenings.
- [Norm just won't be in it](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-07-10-norm-just-won-t-be-in-it/) — Norm Gallagher of the Builders Labourers' Federation has become a folk hero, condemned by the Prime Minister, Premier, and ACTU president, lacerated by The Age, thundered against by The Herald, yet commanding devoted front-line troops who have blocked $8 million of work at the Melbourne Cricket Ground and cost Victoria $150,000 in police protection in a single week.
- [Minding your pees in queues](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-07-24-batmans-melbourne-minding-your-pees-in-queues/) — Boy George has made gender identification nearly impossible, males wear dresses, girls use male deodorants, shoulders are wider on women than men, and a friend waited five minutes in the wrong lavatory queue at the MCG. Keith Dunstan offers a detective's guide: check the jeans, the tops, the sneakers, the earring, the handbag, the posture and the newspaper page they start reading from.
- [A National Trust for our slang](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-07-31-batmans-melbourne-a-national-trust-for-our-slang/) — The new Australian Pocket Oxford Dictionary has arrived with bonzer, bosker, chunder, the trifecta and "bottom of the harbour", but Dunstan finds bosker already extinct, turps endangered, ging unknown to anyone under 30, and proposes that the National Trust should take charge of Australian slang with an A-B-C grading system before the remaining riches of the ocker repertoire disappear forever.
- [I just lap up this computer](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-08-07-batmans-melbourne-i-just-lap-up-this-computer/) — Following the April instalment on his Tandy TRS80 desktop, Keith Dunstan has acquired a Tandy TRS80 Model 100 lap computer, small enough for a briefcase, operable on a plane or on the dunny, and rapturously reports its built-in software, Big Ben chimes, Find function for phone numbers and the astonishing ability to zap copy over any telephone in the world.
- [The problem of the Woo Factor](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-08-21-batmans-melbourne-the-problem-of-the-woo-factor/) — The Woo Factor, the unnecessary gunk added to products to beguile the buyer, is worst in hotels: bathroom telephones by the dunny, automatic refrigerators that register instantly on your bill, mirrors on the ceiling, 2113 slot machines and four-poster beds as big as a squash court at Caesar's Palace. Keith Dunstan proposes a hotel that offers only a comfortable bed, adequate light, a working shower, and no refrigerator.
- [John Bull's vineyard born anew](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-08-28-batmans-melbourne-john-bull-s-vineyard-born-anew/) — Victoria once called itself "John Bull's Vineyard" and in 1894–95 had 12,265 hectares under vine; phylloxera, depression and wowserism nearly wiped it out. Now, after six annual Victorian Winemakers Exhibitions in what were once temperance halls, Roy Moorfield's 48-winery showcase at the Victoria Coffee Palace shows the inferiority complex has gone, Lindeman has revived the "Matthew Lang" label, Seppelts has released "Victorian Wine," and San Francisco is booked for 1986.
- [The action at the Paris end](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-09-04-the-action-at-the-paris-end/) — Victoria legalised brothels in June 1984, giving them 12 months to relocate or obtain council permits, triggering a battle over King's Place ("Cain Lane"), a Collins Street establishment on the 15th floor charging up to $150 for "fantasy," and vivid history of Madame Brussells' garden labyrinth, Annie Wilson's Boccaccio House, and the parliamentary mace that vanished on the night of 8 October 1891.
- [A lament for the All Australian Car](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-09-11-batmans-melbourne-a-lament-for-the-all-australian-car/) — Keith Dunstan proposes a bronze statue of an FJ Holden at Fisherman's Bend to mourn the passing of the genuine Australian car, recalling the 1948 launch under Ben Chifley, the awe it inspired in Melbourne streets, and the humiliation of discovering Danish "Commodores" that turned out to be German Opels; now GM-H is replacing its six-cylinder engine with Japanese Nissan units, Ford is in bed with Mazda, and the world car will be owned by Japan.
- [Melbourne's crisis — the vanishing herd instinct](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-09-18-batmans-melbourne-melbournes-crisis-the-vanishing-herd-instinct/) — Melbourne is losing its famous herd instinct, VFL crowds are down 7.6 percent and 240,000 on 1983, harness racing averages have slumped from 23,400 (1947–48) to 8,200, and greyhound attendance fell 33 percent between 1977 and 1983. Meanwhile the Arts Centre is booming, 72,000 visited the Picasso exhibition in 29 days, and 600 paid $3.50 just to attend an ABC rehearsal.
- [I would like you to meet my LISIM...](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-09-25-batmans-melbourne-i-would-like-you-to-meet-my-lisim/) — Senator Harradine's private member's bill and the ABC's troubles over benefits for homosexual partners expose a gap in English, there is no good word for a live-in unmarried partner. Keith Dunstan coins LISIM (Living In Sin Illegal Mate), proposes a LISIM column in newspapers alongside Births, Deaths and Engagements, and campaigns for an official two-year "lisimit" before benefits are paid.
- [Comics: movies made with ink and paper](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-10-02-batmans-melbourne-comics-movies-made-with-ink-and-paper/) — Comic art has taken on grand respectability, Sydney has Comic Kingdom, Melbourne has Minotaur and Space Age Books, and Australian quarterly Inkspots (fifth issue, 5000 print run) is fielding orders from England for 3000 copies. Colin Paraskevas of Minotaur explains the adult-comic renaissance that began with Epic magazine, while 20-year-old artist Fil Barlow argues that sophisticated comics are "low-budget films, all I need is ink and paper."
- [How the Colliwobbles flattened the Magpies](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-10-09-batmans-melbourne-how-the-colliwobbles-flattened-the-magpies/) — Collingwood, unbeaten since 1958, fell to the Colliwobbles again when Essendon won the preliminary final by 133 points, the greatest preliminary final margin ever, after commentator Lou Richards predicted a great Magpie victory. Coach John Cahill resigned, joining a list of 62 coaches interred since 1973 as club life expectancy drops to 18 months; Dunstan proposes coaches be placed under the protection of the conservation ministry.
- [The other Marconi's marvellous miracle](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-10-16-batmans-melbourne-the-other-marconis-marvellous-miracle/) — Joseph Cornelius Marconi of Bulimba, Brisbane, launched Iguana Brand Goanna Salve in 1910, claiming it cured rheumatism, lumbago, sciatica, eczema, catarrh, ulcers, piles and more, the King of Tonga recently wired Brisbane for four dozen bottles after a knee swollen from a stair fall was cured overnight. Current owner Euan Murdoch ("The Great Goanna") explains how bushies rendered goanna fat on galvanised iron angled at 45 degrees, though today barely a whiff of goanna remains in the tin.
- [Business deals that are hard to swallow](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-10-23-batmans-melbourne-business-deals-that-are-hard-to-swallow/) — The businessmen's breakfast is spreading, the American Chamber of Commerce in Australia celebrated its 500th breakfast briefing last month, and Campbell Soups president Gordon McGovern invited press to 7.30am Hilton sessions after rising at 4am. Keith Dunstan resists: breakfast is a time for meditation, the mind is at its most savage, and nothing civilised should ever be decided at that hour. His proposed solution, deal-making at jogging tracks, comparing pulse rates at the end.
- [How to survive until December 2](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-10-30-batmans-melbourne-how-to-survive-until-december-2/) — The eight-week federal election campaign has Keith Dunstan suffering from "Panfophobiabesmdesondeb", an inability to read large headlines. This is Australia's 38th election since federation, its ninth legislature, the ALP is spending $5 million on ads, and 663 hours of broadcast time were sold in 1975. His survival kit: throw alien conversation-stoppers at people, tune into ABC FM for Bach cantatas after 7pm, and paste the kit on the refrigerator for all emergencies.
- [Melbourne agonises over its super Moomba](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-11-06-batmans-melbourne-melbourne-agonises-over-its-super-moomba/) — Victoria's 150th birthday celebrations begin on November 17, but reaching this point has been agonising. MacPherson Robertson gave £140,000 for the centenary in 1934, funding the MacRobertson Girls High School, a bridge and an air race. The 150th started under Sir John Holland, survived a government change and board spill, then under Ranald Macdonald shaped into 26 hectares of Westgate Park, a Gallery of Sport at the MCG, Spoleto festival for Melbourne in October 1985, the Great Victorian Bike Ride, and world championship cricket under lights.
- [The great leap forward into history](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-11-13-batmans-melbourne-the-great-leap-forward-into-history/) — Melbourne is in the grip of a nostalgia boom, the Old Melbourne Hotel (bluestone from a demolished Fitzroy Methodist chapel, authentic Victorian squeaks), the Windsor after an $11 million Oberoi restoration, and the crown jewel Menzies at Rialto ($50 million, two 1890s buildings with an atrium and a Royal Suite at $600 a day featuring a $30,000 Steinway, gold taps and His-and-Hers bathrooms). The Historic Buildings Council fought to preserve the 1890 corrugated iron urinal shells behind the galleries, but the finest fin de siècle porcelain has quietly vanished.
- [Cricket as the game is written](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-11-13-cricket-as-the-game-is-written/) — A review of Bat and Pad, compiled by Pat Mullins and Philip Derriman (Oxford University Press, $25), a collection of writings on Australian cricket from 1804 to 1984 with a foreword by Bob Hawke. Neville Cardus described Bradman reeling off runs while "Woodfull was as much taken for granted as Kreisler's accompanist," and a 1838 Sydney match produced the complaint about "low slang and insulting remarks." A Bob Menzies courtroom anecdote on the cricketophile judge is the book's high point.
- [The full bottle on Australian wine](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-11-20-batmans-melbourne-the-full-bottle-on-australian-wine/) — Len Evans launched the third edition of his Complete Book of Australian Wine (Lansdowne, $39.95, 791 pages) at the Windsor Hotel, delivering a winemaker's tasting note on himself ("Vintage 1930 ... excessively full in body ... inclined on opening to salacity") before warning that only 3–5 percent of Australian wine is quality and that the federal government's "silvertails" tax policy, 10 cents on a cask, $1.50 on a bottle, was pushing small Victorian makers to the verge of bankruptcy.
- [A roller-coaster ride with Xavier](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-11-27-batmans-melbourne-a-roller-coaster-ride-with-xavier/) — Keith Dunstan's friendship with Xavier Herbert was wildly exhilarating but dangerous, a 12-page letter dissecting him "brain cell by cell" was followed a fortnight later by "Hello. Don't worry about that letter. I was just testing you." Herbert typed the entire 850,000-word Poor Fellow My Country on a 1927 Remington with pop-up keys, kept the only copy in a fireproof gas stove, and when Collins finally published it he won the Miles Franklin Award, then told the gathering he should never have accepted it and called the chairman a silly old fool.
- [The case of the sulking cricket pitch](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-12-04-batmans-melbourne-the-case-of-the-sulking-cricket-pitch/) — Cricket pitches are as mysterious and unfathomable as old wines, the WACA wicket prompted 500,000 words after the first test. Keith Dunstan proposes a Costigan royal commission to investigate the personalities of pitches: the Gabba uses black soil from Goodna (adjacent to the local mental asylum), the SCG soil from Bulli powders and takes spin, the Adelaide Oval is ultra-right-wing and unyielding. The MCG sold 2000 pewter urns of original 1853–1983 wicket soil at $390 each. The current MCG pitch is sulking, it doesn't like pyjama cricket and is on strike.
- [A burning desire to find another pub](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-12-11-batmans-melbourne-a-burning-desire-to-find-another-pub/) — The Eureka flag has been so captured by Norm Gallagher and the Builders' Laborers' Federation that Ballarat citizens despair of reclaiming it. For the 130th anniversary, the Eureka Re-enactment Committee burnt down a real Bentley's Eureka Hotel, bark roof, timber uprights, full Eureka Hotel sign, built in a fortnight from two wrecked houses at Sovereign Hill. More than 3000 people watched it burn magnificently for over an hour; afterwards the march to Bakery Hill re-enacted the monster meeting of 10,000 miners, though the original Bakery Hill is now occupied by a McDonald's restaurant.
- [John Brown's 50 innovative vintages](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-12-18-batmans-melbourne-john-browns-50-innovative-vintages/) — At Mietta's restaurant in Melbourne, the four wine-loving sons of Brown Bros patriarch John Brown celebrate his 50th vintage, recalling Dunstan's first visit to Milawa in 1959 when he became a wine addict on a cabernet shiraz mondeuse that later sold for a shilling and was declared nearly the best red wine an American visitor ever tasted; now Brown handles 35 grape varieties including tarrango, chardonnay and sauvignon blanc, and is developing Australia's highest vineyard at 800 metres near Whitfield in the Upper King Valley.
- [Victoria's great cycle crusade](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1984/1984-12-25-batmans-melbourne-victorias-great-cycle-crusade/) — The inaugural Great Victorian Bike Ride, 850km from Wodonga to Melbourne over nine days, with 3100 cyclists including 70 schools and 700 children as part of Victoria's 150th anniversary celebrations, becomes the biggest mass migration across Victoria since the Gold Rush, drawing middle-aged women, a 70-year-old who cycled to Brisbane and the Gobi Desert, enormous bums in spandex, a street-theatre troupe's paddock wedding, a bride on an exercise bike with a parasol and crocodile, and a finale where police closed the Tullamarine Freeway for the first time in history.
- [Good Lord! — or, an appeal to Mr Packer on a silly cut-off](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1985/1985-07-28/) — An open letter to Kerry Packer protesting Channel Nine's threatened withdrawal of cricket television coverage, arguing Australians are so devoted to the sport that any government permitting its removal from free-to-air TV would face electoral consequences.
- [Worm Fans Rout Norm](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1985/1985-09-27/) — A wry observation on Melbourne's graffiti war over imprisoned BLF leader Norm Gallagher, whose "Free Norm" slogans rivals were altering by turning the N into a W, prompting a wish for a CSIRO spray that could erase all such propaganda from the city's walls.
- [The Gallery of Sport Waits for Norm](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1985/1985-12-06/) — A wry lament over the Victorian Gallery of Sport at the MCG, still unfinished after months of BLF stoppages, demarcation disputes, and a walkout triggered by Premier John Cain's site visit, with completion now pushed to April 1986 at a cost overrun of $1.5 million.
- [Elephants Return to the Fold](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-01-24/) — Hildegard Kamphausen, owner of the Chateau Wyuna restaurant at Mt Evelyn, acquired a deconsecrated 1909 Church of Christ from Montrose and had it moved two and a half kilometres to her property, transforming it into a wedding chapel booked months in advance.
- [Herman Schneider's Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-01-25/) — A profile of Swiss-born Melbourne restaurateur Herman Schneider, whose supposedly sacred Sunday off from running Two Faces in South Yarra and Roesti in Hardware Street was inevitably eaten up by market runs, wine tastings, and anxious checks on both restaurants.
- [Hector Crawford's Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-02-14/) — A profile of Hector Crawford and soprano Glenda Raymond, the Melbourne entertainment power couple whose Sunday tennis club on Toorak Road attracted judges, academics and portrait painters, followed by an evening screening Crawford Productions footage for the Nine Network.
- [As Organic and Good Earth as All Hell](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-02-28-2/) — A visit to the Red Hill Market on the Mornington Peninsula, the monthly produce and craft market that began in 1976 with 22 stalls and by its tenth anniversary had grown to 210, drawing crowds from across Victoria and as far as Adelaide.
- [Peter Russell-Clarke's Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-05-30/) — A Good Weekend "My Sunday" profile of Peter Russell-Clarke at Soho, his century-old farm on Victoria's Bellarine Peninsula, where cooking experiments, Queenscliff fish, long lunches and a mob of more than fifty peacocks define his country weekends.
- [David Penman's Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-07-26/) — A Good Weekend "My Sunday" profile of David Penman, Anglican Archbishop of Melbourne, tracing his weekend from midnight NBC news to parish rounds, Wimbledon tennis, and his growing collection of more than 40 wombat figurines.
- [Frank Little's Sunday](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/1986/1986-12-12/) — A Good Weekend "My Sunday" profile of Frank Little, Catholic Archbishop of Melbourne, whose Sundays run to three or four different homilies, an Italian Mass he preaches in Italian, and a Monday golf game at Metropolitan that recently ended when he stepped off the sixth tee.
- [The Victorian art of columnising](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/bulletin/1995/1995-08-22-the-victorian-art-of-columnising/) — Keith Dunstan tours the mansions of Toorak and finds the suburb's latest fashion is neo-classical columns, tracing its architectural fads from mock Tudor through modernism and "Fortress Toorak" to the Greco-Roman revival of the 1990s.
- [This street was made for walking](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/this-street-was-made-for-walking/) — A defence of the pedestrianised Swanston Walk against councillors pushing to reopen it to traffic, citing survey figures showing it as the busiest pedestrian corner in Melbourne and the return of retailers like Levi Strauss and Nike.
- [The happy thwack of cash on willow](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/the-happy-thwack-of-cash-on-willow/) — A meditation on cricket's transformation from a game of beautifully organised boredom, best enjoyed dozing at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, into a business fought over by players threatening strike action for a share of ballooning sponsorship money.
- [Harbor no grudge, it's better here; The bay and me](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/harbor-no-grudge-its-better-here/) — A Boxing Day case for Port Phillip Bay over its more celebrated rival, touring favourite spots from Sea Winds and Point Nepean to the Sorrento ferry and a flathead-fishing trip with mate Doug Crittenden.
- [Moombas and shakers](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/moombas-and-shakers/) — A profile of the Wittingslow family, the fairground dynasty who have run Moomba's rides and sideshows since patriarch Tom Wittingslow started out guessing weights at Penny Land in 1932, and who now stage the festival itself.
- [A new clutch of ugly ducklings blots the cityscape](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/a-new-clutch-of-ugly-ducklings-blots-the-cityscape/) — A nomination round for Melbourne's ugliest sights, from the Foxtel and Optus advertising signs looming over the historic Young and Jackson's Hotel to the kitsch interior of the new Imax Theatre and the warring columns of 101 Collins Street.
- [On the right track at last](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/on-the-right-track-at-last/) — The Lilydale-Warburton Rail Trail opens along a disused line closed by Henry Bolte in 1964, part of a growing Victorian movement converting old railway corridors into 36 kilometres of bush trail free of motor vehicles.
- [Once a vision, now a site for sore eyes](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/once-a-vision-now-a-site-for-sore-eyes/) — The gutted, empty Southern Cross Hotel four years after the Nauru Government's redevelopment plans collapsed, and a look back at the lively Eastern Market it replaced in the 1960s, the market where C.J. Dennis's Sentimental Bloke first met Doreen.
- [After 500 kilometres, still the kings (and queens) of the road](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/after-500-kilometres-still-the-kings-and-queens-of-the-road/) — The 15th Great Victorian Bike Ride brings 2100 cyclists 500 kilometres from Wahgunyah to Melbourne, among them 83-year-old veteran Alan "Curly" Hartup and the ride's youngest finisher, nine-year-old Anna Clements.
- [Obituary: Richard Cudlipp](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/obituary-richard-cudlipp/) — An obituary for advertising executive Dick Cudlipp, who rose to managing director of George Patterson Bates in 1965, drove Carlton and United Breweries' campaign against the Courage Brewery, and later became a Western District cattle and vineyard grazier.
- [Joy of sport lost in a country that takes it far too seriously](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/joy-of-sport-lost-in-a-country-that-takes-it-far-too-seriously/) — Reflects on Australia's outsized reaction to the 2010-11 Ashes loss under Ricky Ponting, arguing the country has forgotten that sport, unlike genuine disasters such as Cyclone Tracy, is meant to be enjoyed regardless of the result.
- [Plagues be upon us, let's hope for no divine retribution](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/plagues-be-upon-us-lets-hope-for-no-divine-retribution/) — A mock-biblical catalogue of Melbourne's afflictions during a wet 2010, led by a possum population boom under the Wildlife Act, and running through cars, mobile phones, football and noisy restaurants via the ten plagues of Exodus.
- [It's crunch time for Melbourne: we need a congestion tax](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/its-crunch-time-for-melbourne-we-need-a-congestion-tax/) — Argues Melbourne should follow London and Stockholm in adopting a congestion tax to break the city's addiction to the motor car, citing Bicycle Victoria figures on the rising share of peak-hour commuter cyclists.
- [Swear fines a nonsense when invective is so ineffective](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/swear-fines-a-nonsense-when-invective-is-so-ineffective/) — Marks new Victorian on-the-spot fines for swearing by recalling editor Michael Davie's landmark 1979 decision to print an obscenity in The Age, and proposes Paul Keating chair an inquiry into supplying Australians with fresh invective.
- [All I know about ethics, I learned at sword-point](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/all-i-know-about-ethics-i-learned-at-sword-point/) — Recalls a career of manufactured tabloid outrage, from a fake letters-page furore over Myer's window mannequins to a night spent hiding in a wardrobe from a sword-wielding husband, prompted by reflecting on the collapse of the News of the World.
- [Once, footy dominated our lives. Now, things are much worse](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/once-footy-dominated-our-lives-now-things-are-much-worse/) — Surveys the exponential growth of Australian Football League saturation since Keith Dunstan and Douglas Wilkie founded the Anti-Football League in 1967, from a single Saturday afternoon competition to year-round coverage, gambling and coaching sackings.
- [Obituary: Walter Joseph Hauser](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/obituary-walter-joseph-hauser/) — An obituary for Walter Hauser, one of the touring Vienna Mozart Boys' Choir singers stranded in Melbourne by the outbreak of war in 1939, who was taken in by Archbishop Daniel Mannix and went on to a career as an industrial chemist and Keith Dunstan's regular bridge partner.
- [Oh, for the daily thud on my lawn](https://keithdunstan.org/articles/the-age/oh-for-the-daily-thud-on-my-lawn/) — A tribute to the ritual of reading a printed daily newspaper in bed each morning, tracing Keith Dunstan's own newspaper family history against the decades-long death toll of Melbourne mastheads and Rupert Murdoch's prediction that print itself would be gone by 2020.
